- Incendios Incertidumbre y angustia entre los miles de evacuados en los pueblos amenazados de Madrid: "Hoy estamos aquí, mañana no lo sabemos"
Hay incendios que se cuentan con cifras. Hectáreas calcinadas, medios desplegados y personas desalojadas o confinadas. Pero también existen aquellos incendios que solo se entienden cuando los miras de cerca. El miércoles por la noche, camino del pueblo abulense de Burgohondo, punto cero de todo el desastre, el cielo se iba tiñendo poco a poco de un naranja intenso.
Al principio era solamente un simple reflejo en el horizonte, hasta que después se convirtió en una capa inquietante sobre la que se posaba una inmensa lengua de fuego dibujada sobre la sierra. Una imagen hipnótica, irreal incluso, hasta el momento en el que se percibía que detrás de todo aquello había casas, montes y personas.
En el polideportivo municipal de Burgohondo, transformado en refugio más que improvisado, desalojados y voluntarios compartían la mirada fija hacia la montaña. No se hablaba demasiado hasta que el silencio se rompió con el llanto de un bebé. Un lamento que bastó para poner sobre aquel paisaje el reflejo del miedo de todo un pueblo que, mientras el fuego avanzaba, lo único que podía hacer era esperar sin nada más que poder hacer.
Ya de madrugada, aún continuaba ese tono anaranjado de la noche. Solo siete kilómetros después, en Navaluenga, la escena cambió. El pueblo , confinado por el peligro que suponía estar fuera de casa, había convertido una escuela en su punto de reunión y encuentro. Allí vecinos de todas las edades conversaban mientras veían pasar las horas. Entre camiones de la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME) y las siluetas de aquellos que decidieron pasar la noche dentro de sus coches, coexistían las risas y las dudas sobre cuando acabaría toda esta situación. Una misma duda que sobrevolaba entre cada conversación.
Volvió a salir el sol y el humo se hizo notar. Una espesa neblina se suspendió sobre el asfalto y el cielo, yéndose directamente a los ojos y a la nariz. El fuego ya no se veía pero estaba ahí. Solamente bastaba con fijarse en las enormes montañas.
Ya con la noticia de la confirmación del nivel 3 de emergencia nacional el incendio pasaba a un nuevo plano en el que cada uno debía aportar su pequeño grano de arena.
75 kilómetros más cerca de la ciudad de Madrid, convertidos en una pequeña y nueva odisea entre carreteras cortadas por la Guardia Civil y desvíos constantes, el humo seguía siendo el protagonista. Villamanta, el siguiente destino, convirtió su polideportivo en la estancia temporal de cientos de personas evacuadas de Villa del Prado y otros municipios del suroeste de la Comunidad de Madrid. Allí la tragedia tenía rostro. Personas mayores que habían saludo de sus casas con lo puesto. Familias que llevaban casi dos días sin tener información alguna sobre como habían quedado sus hogares ni cuando podrían volver a ellos. Voluntarios con un lema: "Trata a los demás como te gustaría que te trataran a ti», como afirmó Ángel Ramírez que pasó más de 24 horas sin dormir para ayudar a todos los desalojados en Villamanta. E incluso decenas de perros que ladraban no pudiendo comprender por qué habían dejado sus casas atrás.
Pero el calor era sofocante. El murmullo constante se mezclaba con el polvo que levantaban las carreras de los voluntarios que querían llegar a tiempo a toda costa. Conocer esas historias escondidas detrás de cada litera, en donde se posaba la incertidumbre.
Marlene había pasado la noche sobre el suelo del pabellón. "Sí, dormimos aquí, así, en el suelo", contaba resignada. Llevaba horas esperando una noticia que nunca terminaba de llegar. "Nos acaban de decir que todavía no podemos volver. Todo depende del incendio. Como está haciendo mucho aire, sigue avanzando". items.body_text:
El Ayuntamiento de Sevilla comienza este domingo las obras de reasfaltado de la avenida de Carlos V
Los trabajos se acometerán hasta el próximo viernes 31 de julio priorizando el horario nocturno para minimizar el impacto sobre la movilidad en el Prado de San Sebastián
Nuevas obras en Sevilla. En este caso, en un entorno tan transitado por vehículos y peatones como el Prado de San Sebastián. El Ayuntamiento de Sevilla comienza este domingo 26 de julio el reasfaltado de la avenida de Carlos V, unos trabajos cuya ... culminación está prevista el viernes 31. La actuación responde al mal estado en que se encontraba el firme de la vía, que presentaba numerosas imperfecciones y cuarteamientos que suponían un peligro para la circulación de vehículos.
Desde el Consistorio destacan que estas obras suponen que se completa el reasfaltado de todo el eje formado por las avenidas Menéndez Pelayo, El Cid y Carlos V, cuyos dos primeros tramos ya cuentan con el pavimento renovado «tras décadas de abandono». En ese sentido, el delegado de Urbanismo y Medio Ambiente, Juan de la Rosa, ha destacado que se trata de una «importantísima avenida de la ciudad que conecta diferentes zonas y facilita el acceso al centro histórico», y en la que además confluyen numerosas líneas de autobuses, «por lo que es fundamental mejorar el pavimento para conseguir mayor seguridad para conductores y usuarios».
Durante los trabajos se priorizará el horario nocturno para minimizar el impacto sobre la movilidad y garantizar la fluidez del tráfico durante el día. Está previsto el corte total al tráfico rodado de la avenida de Carlos V, en el tramo comprendido entre Menéndez Pelayo y la Borbolla, desde el próximo domingo 26 al viernes 31 de julio en horario nocturno, esto es, de 22.00 a 6.00 horas (excepto domingo 26, que será de 19.00 a 6.00 horas).
Por su parte, el servicio de Tussam adaptará sus recorridos al horario e itinerario alternativo establecido: Menéndez Pelayo, Manuel Bermudo Barrero, San Sebastián, José Mª Osborne, Diego de Riaño, Av. de Málaga, Juan de Mata Carriazo, Av. de la Borbolla, Av. de Portugal, Av. del Cid, Menéndez Pelayo. Asimismo, la calle Diego de Riaño (en el tramo Av. de Portugal-Av. Carlos V y José Mª Osborne-Av. Carlos V) quedan en «fondo de saco» con acceso únicamente a residentes.
Contrato de conservación
Esta actuación se enmarca dentro del Plan de Mejora de Pavimento y Asfalto, cuya dotación económica ha aumentado un 43% respecto al año anterior. Juan de la Rosa ha explicado que el plan «se enmarca en un refuerzo histórico del contrato de conservación de pavimentos de la Gerencia de Urbanismo, que contará con una dotación anual de 20 millones de euros; es decir, más del doble que el contrato que nos encontramos al inicio del mandato». El delegado ha recordado que la partida ha pasado de los 8 millones que destinaba el PSOE a 10, después a 14 y ahora alcanza los 20 millones, lo que supone un incremento del 43% respecto al contrato vigente en 2024-2025.
«Recuperar el asfalto de la ciudad es una de nuestras prioridades. Sevilla necesitaba muchas y grandes actuaciones de mejora del asfalto, puesto que, durante mucho tiempo, numerosas calles han sufrido el abandono de gobiernos anteriores. Seguimos poniendo fin a esa situación gracias a la planificación y la inversión de este equipo de gobierno», ha señalado De la Rosa.
El nuevo contrato refuerza también la capacidad operativa: de las dos empresas que trabajaban en estos servicios se ha pasado a tres, lo que permite cubrir mejor el nivel de trabajo que requiere una ciudad como Sevilla. El plan incluye además una mejora estratégica con la división de la ciudad en tres grandes sectores operativos. La actuación en la avenida Carlos V se localiza en el sector que comprende los distritos Sur, Nervión, Cerro-Amate y San Pablo-Santa Justa.

Detenido un joven por cometer diez robos violentos contra personas vulnerables
La detención se produjo tras una persecución por el barrio de La Coma de Valencia donde un grupo de personas trató de evitar el traslado
Valencia
Agentes de la Policía Nacional han detenido en Paterna (Valencia) a un joven de 20 años como presunto autor de diez delitos de robos con violencia a personas vulnerables, dos robos con fuerza, tres hurtos, un delito contra la seguridad vial y tres delitos de ... resistencia a agentes de la autoridad cometidos desde el mes de junio en la provincia de Valencia y Murcia.
La detención del joven, que ya ha ingresado en prisión, se produjo tras una persecución por el barrio valenciano de La Coma donde un grupo de personas intentaron impedir su traslado a dependencias policiales, según ha informado la Jefatura en un comunicado.
Las investigaciones se iniciaron por parte de agentes adscritos a la Brigada Local de Policía Judicial de Paterna tras tener conocimiento de una serie de robos con violencia cometidos desde el mes de junio en las localidades valencianas de Paterna, Godella, Burjassot, San Antonio de Benagéber y Cartagena (Murcia), cuyas víctimas son personas vulnerables, menores de edad y personas de avanzada edad, contra las que no dudó en emplear la violencia.
Durante las investigaciones los agentes averiguaron que los robos habrían sido cometidos por un joven que abordaba a sus víctimas con la excusa de preguntarles algo, sustrayéndoles unas veces mediante un fuerte tirón, cadenas o collares de oro, y otras veces con intimidación se apropiaba de sus terminales móviles y patinetes eléctricos.
En una ocasión, el sospechoso al parecer abordó a un menor de edad al cual intimidó mediante amenazas para que le diera el teléfono móvil, otra vez, se acercó a un hombre que se encontraba sentado en un banco con la excusa de pedirle un euro, tras lo cual le exigió que le diera todo lo que tenía bajo amenaza de muerte, y a varias víctimas les dio un fuerte tirón de la cadena o collar de oro, llegándolas a lesionar.
Los investigadores identificaron al sospechoso, que resultó ser un delincuente habitual y que tenía en vigor dos reclamaciones judiciales, por lo que establecieron un dispositivo de localización y detención.
Finalmente, y tras «una ardua» labor para localizarlo, ya que el sospechoso contaba con una gran cobertura por parte de vecinos y conocidos en el barrio de La Coma (Paterna) para sus huidas y ocultación, los agentes lo interceptaron tras una persecución por dicho vecindario, deteniéndolo como presunto autor de diez delitos de robo con violencia e intimidación, dos robos con fuerza, tres hurtos, un delito contra la seguridad vial y tres delitos de resistencia a agentes de la autoridad.
En el momento del arresto un numeroso grupo de personas intentaron impedir su traslado a dependencias policiales, por lo que tuvieron que acudir varías patrullas de las Comisarías de Paterna y Burjassot para evitar que la situación se agravara. El arrestado, con antecedentes policiales, ha pasado a disposición judicial, decretándose su ingreso en prisión provisional. Además, se han recuperado dos patinetes eléctricos.

items.title: Fajardo y la recuperación de Abde: «Evoluciona muy positivamente»
items.summary: Uno de los nombres propios durante la larga comparecencia de Ángel Haro y Manu Fajardo ante los medios de comunicación en el acto de presentación de Diego Conde, Fran García y Facundo Bernal como nuevos jugadores del Real Betis fue el de Ez Abde. El extremo marroquí ha iniciado la pretemporada 26-27 recuperándose de la lesión que sufrió con Marruecos ante Noruega en el último encuentro de preparación previo al Mundial y que desgraciadamente le impidió competir por su país en la cita mundialista.
items.body_text:
Real Betis
Fajardo y la recuperación de Abde: «Evoluciona muy positivamente»
El director deportivo del Betis destaca y agradece la profesionalidad del marroquí: «Desde el momento que cayó lesionado ha trabajado día y noche para estar cuanto antes»
Uno de los nombres propios durante la larga comparecencia de Ángel Haro y Manu Fajardo ante los medios de comunicación en el acto de presentación de Diego Conde, Fran García y Facundo Bernal como nuevos jugadores del Real Betis fue el de Ez Abde. El ... extremo marroquí ha iniciado la pretemporada 26-27 recuperándose de la lesión que sufrió con Marruecos ante Noruega en el último encuentro de preparación previo al Mundial y que desgraciadamente le impidió competir por su país en la cita mundialista. Este proceso de recuperación avanza y, según el director deportivo del conjunto verdiblanco, el de Beni Mellal «evoluciona muy positivamente».
En concreto, Fajardo explicó sobre el proceso de recuperación del marroquí que «cumple a la perfección el timing previsto, entre otras cosas, y creo que hay que poner de manifiesto y agradecer porque desde el momento que cayó lesionado ha trabajado día y noche para estar cuanto antes. Queda afianzar un poquito el golpeo, pero el 'timing' es en base a lo que va marcando nuestros doctores. Y recalcar la profesionalidad de Abde».
Preguntado por plazos y la posibilidad de ver al extremo más pronto que tarde en los entrenamientos junto al resto de sus compañeros y el hecho de ir sumando minutos de competición en partidos de pretemporada, el director deportivo bético se mostró respetuoso con el jugador y cauteloso con los tiempos: «Esa pregunta le corresponde a los jefes de los servicios médicos. A mí, sobre todo por respeto al jugador y también por respeto a vosotros mismos, no me gusta dar información que no controlo al 200%. Como bien sabéis, dentro de un periodo de recuperación hay que ser muy cauteloso, muy respetuoso con los tiempos. Lo que sí te puedo decir que evoluciona muy positivamente».
Más ruido que otra cosa en torno a su futuro
En otro orden de cosas, también se le cuestionó a Manu Fajardo sobre el futuro más cercano de Abde. Después de la gran temporada que realizó durante el curso 25-26, el extremo marroquí ha levantado intereses que podían poner encima de la mesa del Betis cantidades económicas que se acerquen lo máximo posible o alcancen los 60 millones de euros que marca su cláusula de rescisión. Aunque no es menos cierto que todas las partes tenían esperanzas en que disputara el Mundial y fuera uno de los futbolistas destacados del combinado magrebí. Pero, según el director deportivo verdiblanco, de momento sólo es más ruido que otra cosa: «Vosotros lleváis en esta industria inclusive más años que yo. Sabéis que se escuchan muchísimas cosas, muchísimo ruido, entorno, medios, clubes, muchos intereses y de momento de todo lo que hay no es más de eso», sentenció Fajardo.

Jamie Dimon, the most powerful banker in the world: ‘I know Europe doesn’t see the US as a friend, but it is’
The chairman and chief executive officer of JPMorgan cautions that stock markets are trading at elevated valuations amid a backdrop of multiple risks. ‘No one saw the 1974 crisis, the 1987 crash or the housing bubble, but you must be prepared,’ he says in an exclusive interview with EL PAÍS
At Madrid’s Pirámide Building on Paseo de la Castellana, some of Spain’s most important business deals are designed, and the country’s wealthiest individuals come seeking investment opportunities for their money. It is the headquarters of JPMorgan, the world’s largest bank (excluding Chinese firms under state control), and on July 10 the atmosphere was that of a major occasion. Everything was in place, including rose arrangements in the colors of the Spanish and U.S. flags, to welcome “the boss”: none other than Jamie Dimon, the last pre-financial crisis banker still in his position.
Born in New York 70 years ago, Dimon has served as chairman and chief executive officer since 2006. Under his leadership, JPMorgan has become a giant with assets worth $5 trillion. Dimon, who had dined the previous evening with around 20 of Spain’s leading business figures, granted an exclusive interview to EL PAÍS, accompanied by Ignacio de la Colina, the bank’s head in Spain.
He arrived without a tie, with the top buttons of his white shirt undone. His greeting was brisk and executive. He gave the impression that, when you are with him, there is never any time to waste. The interview took place days before JPMorgan released its second-quarter results, during which the bank generated revenues of $57.347 billion, up 27%, while profit rose 41% to $21.155 billion. Never before has a bank earned so much money in three months.
Question. What are your prospects for the second half of the year?
Answer. In general, I don’t focus that much on the short term because it’s prone to conjecture, but so far, so good. My experience, however, tells me there are pivots in life, and no one knows when they will happen. The United States seems to be doing quite well, but there are other problems in the world that could alter that situation.
Q. Which business areas are performing best and which need to improve?
A. Most business areas are doing well. This gentleman [pointing to De la Colina] is doing an unbelievable job in Spain, but when we do deep dives into the situation in other countries or into specific divisions or products, we see that, in some cases, they are not performing as expected. It is important to recognize that we are not great at everything, and that others do some things better than us. Only then can we address our weaknesses.
Q. Will JPMorgan’s growth be purely organic, or are you considering new acquisitions?
A. The important thing is that we can grow 100% organically. Sometimes people underestimate the importance of organic growth, but to achieve it you must hire good professionals and have good systems. That’s what we do across all areas. For example, we have launched a strategy to open 500 branches in small towns in rural areas of the United States. Although we can grow 100% organically, we are always looking at opportunities to grow inorganically as well. You learn a lot when you explore those alternatives, but it should never be an excuse, as it is for some companies, not to grow organically.
Q. A few months ago you said that after certain regulatory reforms you had freed capital and had $20 billion that could be used for acquisitions. Do you have any targets in mind?
A. We are not obliged to spend that money; it is not a self‑imposed limit. If we wanted to, we could move up to $200 billion to finance a new deal, but we are not going to do that. Among other reasons, in the United States we cannot buy a bank. items.title: ‘We’re surviving’: raids deliver a heavy and lasting blow to Hispanic businesses in L.A.
items.summary: In nine commercial corridors frequented by migrants in that city there were nearly $3.2 million in losses in 2025 due to Trump’s aggressive immigration offensive, a UCLA study reveals
items.body_text:
‘We’re surviving’: raids deliver a heavy and lasting blow to Hispanic businesses in L.A.
In nine commercial corridors frequented by migrants in that city there were nearly $3.2 million in losses in 2025 due to Trump’s aggressive immigration offensive, a UCLA study reveals
The arrival of dozens of immigration agents, unleashed to hunt for undocumented migrants, emptied the streets of Pico Rivera, California. In June 2025 residents of this suburb east of Los Angeles began to get used to a scene previously unthinkable: convoys of white trucks with green stripes driving through their avenues again and again. The Border Patrol had set its sights on a sanctuary city for migrants to send a show of force and to foreshadow what would come in other communities across the country. In one of those operations, several agents stopped outside a tire shop near Rosemead Boulevard and tried to detain its workers. Someone livestreamed the raid on Facebook Live and the video went viral immediately. It was the final blow for nearby businesses.
“From there it went down, down, down. We haven’t been able to recover,” laments Roberto Godínez, owner of a convenience store whose sales rely mostly on bottled water, beer and snacks. “We’re surviving as if we were in an economic crisis. From $3,500 in sales a day we now barely reach $1,400. It hardly covers workers’ pay.” Godínez, an immigrant originally from Jalisco, Mexico who has spent most of his 65 years on this side of the border, had hoped the World Cup would give his finances a breather. The tournament, however, took place over 39 days without changing the despondency that settled in the neighborhood after the raids. “People don’t even go out to buy beer,” he says.
What happened to this small business at the start of the Trump administration’s immigration offensive is not an isolated case. Its story sums up that of hundreds of Hispanic-owned businesses in this metropolitan area, hit by the fear sown by the raids. A report from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) concludes that “the June 2025 enforcement surge caused immediate and lasting economic harm” in Latino commercial corridors in the county. In just the first two weeks of June 2025, these establishments recorded 46,000 fewer visits, a drop that translated into estimated accumulated losses of nearly $3.2 million. Even a year later, many owners are still waiting for a recovery that has yet to come.
Blows to wallets and to health
The study focused on 75 Latino entrepreneurs with businesses spread across nine commercial corridors frequented by Hispanic immigrants, including Huntington Park, Whittier, Westlake, Pacoima and the Fashion District. UCLA researchers even documented the impact on foot traffic, which broadly declined in the days after the raids began.
Fifty-nine percent of those interviewed reported income drops greater than 50%, while half said some of their employees stopped coming to work for fear of being detained by immigration agents. As a result, seven out of 10 establishments reduced opening hours or closed temporarily. Many business owners said sales barely covered operating costs and sometimes not even that. This year the outlook has barely changed: 95% acknowledged they were still facing financial difficulties due to the lack of customers. The impact has also been personal. Seventy-six percent of these business owners said they suffered emotional deterioration that ultimately affected their health.
“A year later, many business owners remain in a state of financial vulnerability. Fear, uncertainty and economic pressure continue to erode their health and wellbeing,” said Amada Armenta, co-author of the report and director of UCLA’s Latino Policy and Politics Initiative (LPPI), in a statement. “The loss of customers affected businesses of different sectors and sizes, regardless of their owners’ immigration status.”

items.title: Half a year of terror for Mexico’s press
items.summary: Seven journalists have been murdered since January, adding to a series of direct attacks against local media outlets and reporters across the country. Arrests have been made in only one of the cases
items.body_text:
Half a year of terror for Mexico’s press
Seven journalists have been murdered since January, adding to a series of direct attacks against local media outlets and reporters across the country. Arrests have been made in only one of the cases
The press in Mexico is working under a climate of fear and terror following at least seven journalist murders recorded in the first six months of 2026. The latest victim was Francisco Alejandro Leyva Aguilar, who was killed on Wednesday while eating at a taco stand.
His murder comes just days after Josué Martínez Contreras, 39, was killed on July 16 in the community of San Lucas Atoyatenco, in the municipality of San Martín Texmelucan, Puebla. His 13-year-old son was with him when gunmen riding a motorcycle opened fire. The boy was the one who called emergency services, but there was nothing they could do when they arrived at the scene.
These killings add to the murders of independent journalist and environmental activist Manuel Alejandro Moreno Serna, murdered on July 3 in Zihuatanejo, Guerrero; Veracruz journalist Roxana Berenice Guzmán, who recorded her own kidnapping weeks before her body was found; Luis Ángel López Valdez, murdered on June 11 in Poza Rica, also in Veracruz; Juan David Gámez, killed in Nuevo León in March; and Carlos Castro, who died on January 8, also in Poza Rica.
Oaxaca journalist Francisco Alejandro Leyva Aguilar became the seventh reporter killed in Mexico this year after gunmen shot him dead at a roadside food stall in San Pablo Etla. Leyva, a veteran columnist known for his criticism of the state government, had reported receiving death threats to both state and federal authorities in 2025, but no protective measures were implemented. Press freedom groups have since questioned why officials failed to act despite being aware of the risks he faced
Meanwhile, investigations into the Martínez Contreras case have already begun, according to the Puebla State Attorney General’s Office. However, a video he uploaded to social media last November already showed the harassment he was experiencing from local authorities after he reported the existence of unauthorized connections to the municipal water system and the lack of transparency regarding public funds collected through water-service fees.
According to the recording by the journalist, who was also an academic and lawyer, the municipal president and personnel from Mexico’s National Water Commission (Conagua) came to his home and accused him of failing to pay several water bills. Martínez Contreras showed the camera receipts proving payment and stated that, although he had clarified the situation and presented the documentation, he was still forced to pay what amounted to a “fine” of 6,000 pesos (about $350).
“The crux of this whole matter is that we have not allowed them to run a lucrative business from the water supply [...] What they want is to get rid of me, push me aside,” he says in the video.
The video, which lasts just over five minutes, ends with the following statement: “Remember that it is better to die with the strength of the people than to die on your knees. I tell you this: we are going to fight for our people and for our municipality.”
Following his murder, Reporters Without Borders (RSF) in Latin America raised new questions for the Mexican government regarding the dangers faced by the press in the country: “How many have to die for the authorities to realize their response remains clearly insufficient? Opening an investigation after each murder is simply not enough,” said Artur Romeu, RSF’s regional director. “The Mexican government must be held accountable for the failures in prevention and protection that have allowed these crimes to recur, and present concrete measures to keep these killings from happening.”
The attack on journalist Roxana Berenice Guzmán was also captured on video. Guzmán was the founder of Pulso Informativo del Sureste, a Facebook news page she managed from Nanchital, in southeaste

items.title: Amsterdam’s first WorldPride begins Saturday; City expects 1 million visitors
items.summary: WorldPride, the international LGBTQIA+ event held every two years in a different city, begins today in Amsterdam for the first time.
items.body_text:
Amsterdam’s first WorldPride begins Saturday; City expects 1 million visitors
WorldPride, the international LGBTQIA+ event held every two years in a different city, begins today in Amsterdam for the first time. Queen Máxima opens the event this afternoon in the Vondelpark under the theme Unity. The schedule includes street parties, concerts, a human rights conference, and a Pride March to the Museumplein. The Canal Parade is set to take place halfway through the program.
Pride Amsterdam has already been under way since July 8 and runs through July 29. WorldPride gives the celebration a larger, more international scale with extra attention on the global fight for equal rights for LGBTQIA+ people.
Fifty-three distinctive buildings across the city will be lit in rainbow colors. A grandstand seating 10,000 will be set up on the Prinsengracht for the Canal Parade.
WorldPride has taken place in odd-numbered years since 2017, most recently in Washington, D.C. Amsterdam secured the 2026 edition after a successful bid. The timing coincides with several milestones: the 80th anniversary of human-rights group COC, 30 years of Pride in Amsterdam, and the 25th anniversary of the Netherlands becoming the first country in the world to open civil marriage to same-sex couples.
Siep de Haan co-founded Pride Amsterdam and its boat parade in 1996 with his husband, Peter Kramer, and Ernst Verhoeven. They organized the event “from beginning to end” for its first decade.
In the 1990s Amsterdam, unlike many large Western cities, still had no Pride. Elsewhere, such events often grew from protests against police violence, discrimination and slow legal change. “Amsterdam luckily did not have that ‘handicap,’” De Haan told NOS. "Here, from the 1970s and 1980s, it was already a gay paradise. The rainbow community was visible, and people felt safe. There was a lot of mutual respect.”
The boat parade was created to draw attention and establish Amsterdam as a gay nightlife destination. “Amsterdam is a small city compared to London, New York, and Paris. We needed something unique. This was our way to communicate with society: subtle, without walking with protest signs, but still showing that we are here,” De Haan told the newspaper.
The expected million visitors do not surprise him. “Three years after we started, we were already the third event of Amsterdam. And now we have been standing head and shoulders above for years,” he said, laughing.
Pride has become more political, De Haan said, reflecting wider social debates. He voiced concern over falling LGBTQIA+ acceptance among young people.
University of Amsterdam research earlier this year found that 41 percent of young people do not agree that everyone is equal regardless of whom someone falls in love with.
Pride spokesperson Martijn Albers stressed that the event is more than a party. A special WorldPride solidarity fund is bringing more than 150 activists to the Netherlands for the human-rights conference. The group includes people from countries where homosexuality is banned or where LGBTQIA+ people face serious danger.
“For us, marrying 25 years after the opening of the marriage has almost become self-evident,” Albers said. “For very many people from other countries it is still a dot on the horizon. At such a conference it is special how much you can learn from each other.”

items.title: British man sentenced to 5 years for stabbing tourist, another victim in Amsterdam
items.summary: A 30-year-old British man was sentenced Friday to five years in prison for stabbing two men in separate attacks in the city center, one involving a tourist during a 2022 robbery and the other a 202
items.body_text:
British man sentenced to 5 years for stabbing tourist, another victim in Amsterdam
A 30-year-old British man was sentenced Friday to five years in prison for stabbing two men in separate attacks in the city center, one involving a tourist during a 2022 robbery and the other a 2024 nightlife fight, AT5 reports. Both incidents were ruled attempted manslaughter, with the first also involving violent extortion. The court ordered him to pay a combined 27,000 euros in damages to the victims, with time already spent in pretrial detention to be deducted from the sentence.
On the night of Sept. 20-21, 2022, the man approached a tourist in the Wallengebied and asked where an ATM was. He continued walking with the tourist, then suddenly attacked him in the Prinsenhofssteeg, pulling a knife from his waistband.
The tourist started running but was overtaken on the Oudezijds Achterburgwal, where the man stabbed him in the arm, armpit, and abdomen while shouting “money.”
Then in the early morning of Dec. 1, 2024, the man became involved in a street fight near a nightclub on the Rembrandtplein. After the second victim kicked him and fell, the man stabbed the victim four times. The victim suffered a collapsed lung and blood in his chest cavity, spent a week in the hospital, continues to have ongoing arm pain and has multiple scars.
The court described the tourist as vulnerable. “The complainant was vulnerable, a tourist in a strange city and under the influence of alcohol. The suspect has grossly abused that,” the ruling stated. It also characterized the second attack as senseless nightlife violence.
Police arrested the man a few days after the 2024 stabbing. He was carrying a loaded pistol and had tried unsuccessfully to evade capture by shaving his hair, police said.
He is from Great Britain and was first imprisoned at age 15. He has prior convictions in Australia, Great Britain, and Norway, where a lengthy prison sentence remains outstanding.

items.title: Video: Bright fireball seen across Netherlands, said to be satellite from Musk's SpaceX
items.summary: A bright fireball appeared over parts of the Netherlands around 10:30 p.m. on Friday as a Starlink satellite from Elon Musk’s SpaceX burned up after re-entering Earth’s atmosphere.
items.body_text:
Video: Bright fireball seen across Netherlands, said to be satellite from Musk's SpaceX
A bright fireball appeared over parts of the Netherlands around 10:30 p.m. on Friday as a Starlink satellite from Elon Musk’s SpaceX burned up after re-entering Earth’s atmosphere.
Sightings came from Amsterdam, Utrecht, Almere, Dronten, Arnhem, the Frisian Gaastmeer, Texel, Mijdrecht, and other locations. Satellite expert Marco Langbroek from TU Delft identified the object as Starlink 1541.
“It entered the atmosphere above England and started breaking up and burning up there. That typically happens at altitudes between 90 and 50 kilometers,” Langbroek told NOS.
Langbroek saw it pass over Texel. “The re-entry was expected for this night, but because there was an uncertainty of four hours, it was hard to predict exactly when. I was sitting with a few people on the deck of a sailboat when we saw it, entirely by chance.” He noted, “There was also a vapor trail visible in the atmosphere for minutes. Those are microscopic metal particles left behind in the upper parts of the atmosphere.”
Astronomer Lucas Ellerbroek watched the fireball over Amsterdam. “The bigger such a piece of space debris is, the more fire you see,” he explained.
Much of an object is lost during atmospheric entry, as with meteors. Ellerbroek said, "If you have a rock of a meter, that causes a large fireball, but the remnant that lands on Earth does not have to be larger than a few centimeters. It breaks apart into fragments that are no larger than pebbles.”
Ellerbroek said more details should emerge Saturday morning on whether the satellite completely disintegrated.
But “it has probably burned up completely, although you can never completely rule out that some fragments remained," Ellerbroek said. "Those then presumably came down in Germany or Eastern Europe.”
Only six meteorites have been found in the Netherlands across the centuries. The first landed near Uden in 1840. The latest, recovered near Broek in Waterland in 2017, was a half-kilogram stone that damaged a roof.
Elon Musk’s SpaceX started launching Starlink satellites in 2019. The more than 10,000 relatively small satellites orbit at about 500 kilometers and deliver internet without extensive ground systems.
The network has assisted Ukrainian drones in locating targets during the war with Russia. It was also reportedly used by Iranians when the government restricted internet access. Astronomers criticize the project for occupying limited space around Earth and creating light pollution that interferes with observations of the universe.

items.title: Blood on Her Tongue: A modern vampire tale not for the squeamish
items.summary: Johanna van Veen’s gothic horror Blood on Her Tongue offers up a classic vampire tale with some modern contemplations. The...
items.body_text:
Blood on Her Tongue: A modern vampire tale not for the squeamish
Molly QuellSee more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on GoogleJohanna van Veen’s gothic horror Blood on Her Tongue offers up a classic vampire tale with some modern contemplations.
The book follows Lucy Goedhart as she is called to the ominously named Zwartwater (black water) estate, where her sister has taken ill. In 1887, there isn’t much in the way of medical treatment, but Lucy’s sister Sarah isn’t fighting off a regular illness.
Sarah has become obsessed with a body found in the bog of the vast estate and since interacting with the 300-year-old corpse she has become increasingly incoherent, struggles with taking care of herself and has developed an insatiable hunger.
As Lucy tries desperately to save her sister, she finds that her sister’s husband, her sister’s doctor and childhood friend, and several other characters who are present at the remote manor house all have their own interests and motivations – some as dangerous as whatever condition is plaguing Sarah.
The book is not for those easily bothered by gore. The title – Blood on Her Tongue – is a pretty good indication of what is to come. Van Veen does not shy away from the horror elements, including two separate scenes of eyeball gouging.
Like any good horror novel, the macabre monster is not the scariest part. The threats Lucy faces are from the men surrounding her sister. Her brother-in-law attempts to seduce Lucy while badgering her to send Sarah away to an asylum.
Sarah’s doctor expresses his own interest in Lucy, pushing his vision of the future while supposedly devoting himself to his patient. The mores of 19th-century upper-class society may be the biggest piece of villainy of all.
In the tradition of Dracula, Blood on Her Tongue tells its story through letters, journal entries and newspaper clippings. The personal correspondence adds to the claustrophobia of the work, with everyone limited to an isolated house, but the media reports remind the reader that the world outside does exist.
The work is the second book from Dutch author Johanna van Veen. It was published in 2025 in English and became a USA Today bestseller. Her first book, My Darling Dreadful Thing, was nominated for the Bram Stoker Award for best horror novel. Van Veen grew up in the Netherlands as a triplet, something that influenced her writing about the sisters Lucy and Sarah.
If horror is your thing, Blood on Her Tongue will creep you out and keep you turning the pages.
You can get your copy at the American Book Center.

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on GoogleThe 108th edition of the Nijmegense Vierdaagse (four-day march) ended on Friday, with tens of thousands of walkers being welcomed with flowers by well-wishers.
British walker Simon Brownlee crossed the finishing line ahead of the rest of the walkers for the 27th time, local media reported. Brownlee, who completed the distance before 10am, told local broadcaster Omroep Gelderland that the walk “felt like home”. “I’m happy it is over and I can now relax,” he said.
Wheelchair participant Ronald van Dort was the very first person to finish, picking up his seventh medal for completing the event.
Over 45,000 walkers from 70 countries took part in this year’s series, which is proving increasingly popular among the young. Ten years ago, 7.5% of the walkers were aged 21 to 30, but this year their number rose to over 20%.
This year the event was marred by a fatal shooting just outside the area where the Vierdaagsefeesten, the street festivities accompanying the annual four-day marches, were taking place. One man has been arrested.
The shooting, and other crowd problems, led the organisers to cancel performances by urban scene artists such as Ronnie Flex and Lil’ Kleine because their presence was “attracting the wrong sort of people”, the AD reported.

Dozens of women forced into prostitution by Romanian gang
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on GoogleDozens of women may have been forced into working as prostitutes in Amsterdam’s red light district by a Romanian gang, Dutch police confirmed on Friday.
The statement follows a joint Dutch and Romanian campaign against human trafficking in the area earlier this month. Seven men were arrested during a string of raids on July 14 – four in the Netherlands and three in Romania. All were Romanian nationals.
Shortly after the arrests, police issued a video interview with one of the victims speaking Romanian, which has led more women to come forward and has resulted in other information reaching the police, the statement said.
Police now say they have spoken to several victims and say they believe more women have been trafficked. They too are said to be Romanian.
The women were lured to Amsterdam with the promise of high earnings but found themselves forced into working in brothels and handing over their earnings to the gang. They were also forced to pay “rent” for their rooms.
None of the men had jobs but were big spenders, buying expensive clothes and cars and gambling heavily, the statement said. The gang also treated part of the red light district as their “personal kingdom”.
Four men remain in custody in the Netherlands, one of whom was extradited from Romania. Another man may also be extradited soon, RTL said. They are all suspected of human trafficking and forming a criminal organisation.
According to the Parool, two of the suspects are half brothers aged 44 and 45 who have earlier convictions for trafficking in women in Romania.
More arrests have not been ruled out.
A year ago, Dutch and Romanian police arrested 13 people in a joint investigation into human trafficking and the forced prostitution of Romanian women, mainly in and around Amsterdam.

items.title: Poland bans chaining of dogs and cats
items.summary: President Nawrocki vetoed an earlier version of the bill but has now signed a revised version into law.
items.body_text:
Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
Keeping dogs and cats chained up at home will be banned in Poland from next year, after President Karol Nawrocki signed into law a bill prohibiting the practice.
His decision ends a long-running dispute over the issue, after Nawrocki last year vetoed a previous proposal to ban chaining because it also included what he argued were excessive and unrealistic additional measures on minimum kennel sizes for dogs.
Zawetowana w listopadzie 2025 r. ustawa łańcuchowa była źle przygotowana i przeregulowana, ponieważ nakładała na obywateli obowiązki, których wielu nie byłoby w stanie spełnić.
Dzisiaj otrzymujemy ustawę lepszą, z pozytywnym głosem takich podmiotów jak rolniczy samorząd.… pic.twitter.com/h7kIAI77KR
— Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) July 24, 2026
The new law bans owners from tethering dogs and cats at home. Animals must be kept either inside the house, in a fenced garden or, if that is not possible, in a kennel “large enough for the animal to move freely and satisfy its natural needs”. Dogs kept in kennels must be provided with daily exercise outside of it.
Dogs and cats can still be put on leashes in certain situations, such as when they are being walked, but also during transport, while participating in shows, performances or training, if they are at vets or groomers, or if they represent a danger to humans or other animals.
Now that the bill has been signed by Nawrocki, it will be published in the official Journal of Laws (Dziennik Ustaw), after which it goes into force 12 months later.
The new measures represent a successful second attempt to introduce a leashing ban. A previous bill was approved by parliament last September. However, in December, Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, announced that he was vetoing it.
The president argued that, “although the intention – protecting animals – is just and noble, the law itself was poorly drafted”. In particular, he said that elements introducing minimum sizes for dog kennels were unrealistic and would “harm farmers, breeders and ordinary rural households”.
After an attempt by parliament to overturn the veto failed, legislators went back to the drawing board and, following discussions with the president’s chancellery and animal rights groups, drafted a compromise bill that was approved by parliament earlier this month.
The bill received support from the current ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, as well as most MPs from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), the main opposition party. The far-right Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) voted against it.

items.title: Police and park rangers step up joint patrols in Poland’s Tatras after series of tourist offences
items.summary: Authorities in the national park remind visitors that bathing in lakes and other transgressions can damage the fragile ecosystem.
items.body_text:

Police officers and rangers have stepped up joint patrols in Poland’s mountainous Tatra National Park during the peak summer season, following a spate of rule-breaking including swimming in the park’s lakes and ponds, driving cars and going off marked trails.
Meanwhile, national park authorities have repeated warnings that bathing, littering and breaking other rules can damage the park’s fragile ecosystem.
Local police officers have joined Tatra National Park rangers on patrols on popular tourist routes. On one such patrol last week, officers focused on education and prevention, reminding visitors not to leave marked trails or litter and explaining how to behave safely and responsibly in the mountains.
They also checked that organised groups were accompanied by qualified mountain guides, as required by law. Fines for such offences range from 50 zloty (€11.55) to as much as 1,000 zloty (€231) in the event of environmental damage or multiple offences.
Police said that all visitors encountered during the patrol were complying with the park’s regulations. However, they added that similar patrols would continue on a regular basis.
The Tatra National Park, home to Poland’s highest peaks, and the nearby mountain resort of Zakopane are among the country’s most popular holiday destinations, with crowds taking to park trails in the summer season.
The park, the most visited of Poland’s 23 national parks, welcomed a record 5.3 million visitors in 2025 and offers 275 km of marked hiking trails, including high-altitude routes that connect at several points with the adjacent national park in Slovakia.
🚨 Ukraiński Influencer wjechał nielegalnie samochodem na Morskie oko
🗣️: Jesteśmy pierwszymi ludźmi w historii, którzy wjechali samochodem nad Morskie Oko. To było jedno z miejsc, do których chcieliśmy dotrzeć podczas tej podróży i wszyscy znajomi oraz przyjaciele mówili, że… pic.twitter.com/tA9shZ6Rqk
— Pigułka 💊 (@informacyjnie) May 23, 2026
This season has already seen a number of high-profile cases of transgressions of the park’s strict rules. In May, a Ukrainian social media influencer sparked outrage after driving a sports car along a road closed to traffic to Morskie Oko, a picturesque lake nestled between the mountains.
As a result, he was banned from entering Poland and other Schengen Area countries for five years.
Tourists have also been filmed entering Morskie Oko and other protected lakes and ponds, which is not permitted in the national park. This month, a group of young Dutch tourists were filmed bathing in Przedni Staw Polski in the Valley of the Five Lakes, one of the Tatras’ best-known hiking destinations.
Witnesses repeatedly warned the group that entering the lake was prohibited, but they ignored the warnings, reports Gazeta Wyborcza. Park authorities have responded to such incidents by reminding visitors of the reasons for the strict rules.
“Tatra ponds are incredibly delicate ecosystems. Cosmetics, UV filters, insect repellents, and bacteria entering the water can have a long-lasting impact on its chemical composition and the organisms living in the lakes,” they warned.
A national park in Poland’s southern mountains has completed testing of an electric bus that could replace horse-drawn carriages carrying tourists to a famous lake.

items.title: Polish opposition PiS party set to split, with over 30 MPs being expelled
items.summary: A group centred around former Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki refused to sign a pledge of loyalty demanded by the party.
items.body_text:
Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
More than 30 MPs from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s main opposition party, have effectively resigned after refusing to sign a loyalty pledge, party leader Jarosław Kaczyński has announced.
The dispute centres around a more moderate faction in the party aligned with former prime minister and deputy PiS leader Mateusz Morawiecki, who is one of those now set to be expelled from the party. They have for months been unhappy with PiS’s move in a hard-right direction.
💬 Prezes PiS Jarosław Kaczyński @OficjalnyJK.
👉 Udostępnij pic.twitter.com/bycjE0Yq0f— Prawo i Sprawiedliwość (@pisorgpl) July 24, 2026
“Around 30-something…of our group’s MPs have resigned,” revealed Kaczyński at a press conference on Friday. He added that their departures would be formalised at a meeting of the party’s political committee scheduled for Tuesday next week.
Kaczyński’s announcement came after a deadline expired at midnight on Thursday for its MPs to sign a pledge of loyalty to the party that included a commitment not to be members of any external political associations.
That measure was aimed in particular at an association called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) founded by Morawiecki in April. The former prime minister had always insisted that his organisation was intended as complementary to PiS, rather than a rival to it.
However, many figures in the party saw it as an attempt by Morawiecki to create a separate centre of power, and potentially to use the association as a launchpad for creating his own party ahead of the autumn 2027 parliamentary elections.
The right-wing opposition PiS party has threatened disciplinary action, including exclusion from electoral lists, against dozens of its MPs who have joined a new internal group led by former PM @MorawieckiM and intended to appeal to more moderate voters https://t.co/y62Cm361U2
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 17, 2026
After PiS issued a resolution on Wednesday last week requiring that its parliamentarians pledge to withdraw from any such associations, most of its 186 MPs quickly complied. However, a group of between 30 and 40 who are part of Development Plus refused to do so.
“Everyone knew what they were supposed to sign, and knew the consequences of not signing,” said Kaczyński on Friday. “And so they made the decision they did.”
“In this situation, we cannot view the [Development Plus] association as anything other than a component of a plan…to split our party,” he added. However, although its supporters will now leave PiS, “we want to part ways without any animosity”, said Kaczyński.
After Kaczyński’s announcement, senior figures from Development Plus made clear that no one from their association had resigned from PiS. They had simply not signed the declaration of loyalty demanded by the party.
Later, Morawiecki himself held a press conference in parliament surrounded by his supporters. He claimed that an unnamed “small group of schemers” within PiS had been seeking to turn Kaczyński against him and push him out of the party.
“We fought for the unity of Law and Justice until the very end,” declared Morawiecki, who said that his group included 40 MPs, one senator and three MEPs. However, three of the MPs are not members of PiS, and therefore were not expected to sign the loyalty declaration.

items.title: Serbian Flag on Cocaine Haul from Ecuador is a Clue – Not Proof
items.summary: The Serbian flag displayed on packages of cocaine doesn’t prove the traffickers were linked to Serbia. - but the documented activities of Balkan criminal groups in Ecuador make the possibility worth investigating.
items.body_text:
On July 21, the Italian authorities seized 650 packages with more than 770 kilograms of cocaine at the port of Vado Ligure. The drugs were hidden among pallets of bananas in a refrigerated container from Ecuador.
Concealing cocaine in commercial shipments of fresh fruit, particularly bananas from Ecuador, is a well-known method used by criminal actors, including groups from the Balkans.
The Vado Ligure seizure, therefore, fits a broader pattern of maritime cocaine trafficking into Europe.
In Serbia, however, it wasn’t the size of the seizure or its route that attracted most attention but the Serbian flag displayed on some of the packages.
Although the comments posted under the media reports offer only a snapshot of public opinion, they reveal two recurring reactions.

items.title: Law and Justice Suffers Split Ahead of Poland’s 2027 Election
items.summary: The biggest rupture on the Polish right in many years could sharply reduce PiS’s chances of returning to power in next year’s parliamentary election.
items.body_text:
Law and Justice Suffers Split Ahead of Poland’s 2027 Election
Following a months-long power struggle, more than 30 MPs – including former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki – are set to be expelled from the Law and Justice party, in the biggest rupture seen on the Polish right in many years.
Law and Justice, or PiS, is Poland’s largest opposition party and one of the country’s two dominant political forces, alongside the governing Civic Coalition led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The split could sharply reduce PiS’s chances of returning to power in next year’s parliamentary election.
On early Friday afternoon, PiS leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski announced that “around 30-something” of the party’s 186 MPs had effectively chosen to leave after refusing to sign declarations of loyalty. The documents required them to state that they did not belong to any political associations operating within the party – an obvious reference to Development Plus (Rozwoj Plus), an organisation created by Morawiecki, until now one of PiS’s deputy leaders.
“Everyone knew what they were supposed to sign, and knew the consequences of not signing,” Kaczynski said. “And so they made the decision they did.”
Kaczynski has been PiS’s undisputed leader and chief power broker for more than two decades, selecting loyal candidates for prime minister who largely continued to defer to him once in office. Morawiecki was initially one of them, serving as prime minister between 2017 and 2023.
But in recent years, Morawiecki – an economist, former banker and comparatively moderate conservative – has grown increasingly impatient with Kaczynski’s dominance. He has pushed for changes to both the party’s internal structure and its political program, arguing that PiS was failing to speak convincingly to younger voters and entrepreneurs.
Friday’s rupture was the culmination of months of increasingly open conflict.
“Until the very last moment, we fought for the unity of the Law and Justice camp,” Morawiecki said at a press conference. “We could not accept being forced to sign a loyalty pledge.”
He accused the party leadership of using ultimatums and political blackmail to discard a strategy that had been agreed only recently.
Morawiecki did not formally announce the creation of a new party. He did, however, declare the beginning of “a new chapter in Poland’s political history”, promise a major nationwide tour and announce that his camp would soon present a new political program.
He said his political circle now included 40 MPs (which stands at odds with Kaczynski’s estimate), one senator and three members of the European Parliament, describing it as a “very strong representation”. Its offer, he said, would reach beyond PiS’s traditional base and target young people, entrepreneurs, local-government officials and even some voters currently supporting the governing coalition.
Morawiecki presented his project as a modern, patriotic and pro-state conservative force, capable of responding to social and economic change without falling back on outdated ideas.
The electoral consequences could be enormous. An Opinia24 poll conducted before the split tested precisely such a scenario. With PiS united, the party would receive 23 per cent of the vote, behind Civic Coalition on 31.6 per cent. When respondents were offered a separate Morawiecki-led Rozwoj Plus list, support for PiS fell to 17.7 per cent, while Morawiecki’s group received 6.2 per cent. Civic Coalition remained clearly ahead on 30.9 per cent.
Tusk responded with a single cutting line: “They are fighting so hard for party unity that there won’t be one stone left standing.”
Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski was blunter: “Kaczynski went all in and lost.”

items.title: Week in Review: A Fighting Spirit
items.summary: From Albania’s ‘Flamingo Revolution’ to Turkey’s embattled opposition, BIRN’s premium selection of stories this week tell a fighting mood is visible across south-east Europe, despite the summer heat.
items.body_text:
Week in Review: A Fighting Spirit
New buzz
Turkey’s opposition political scene is heating up. On July 21, Ozgur Ozel announced that he was leaving the main opposition Republican People’s Party, CHP, to establish a new party.
The news followed a crisis triggered two months ago, when a court annulled Ozel’s election as CHP leader at an earlier party congress, restoring his predecessor, Kemal Kilicdaroglu, as leader. Ozel’s new party looks set to take a majority of the CHP’s MPs and voters. But can it be turned into a political force capable of taking on the ruling party?
Read more: New Party Brings Fresh Hope – and Risks – for Turkey’s Embattled Opposition (July 23, 2026)
Wrong incentives
More than two months after the fall of Ilie Bolojan’s cabinet in May, Romania is still waiting for a new government. The wait may prove long.
In his opinion piece for Balkan Insight, Bjorn Anseeuw argues that the crux of the problem in Romania is not institutions or the politicians per se but an incentive structure that rewards avoiding – rather than assuming – political responsibility.
Read more: Romania’s Political Class Sees Rewards in Not Governing (July 20, 2026)
Not for sale
Protests in Albania continue over a planned luxury tourism development on Sazan island and Zvernec, linked to Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner. The slogan “Albania is not for sale” has become one of the rallying cries of the demonstrators.
But, as Evarist Stoja argues in his opinion piece for Balkan Insight, the slogan is often misinterpreted. Protesters are not opposed to investments across the board – simply to those lacking transparency.
Read more: Who Really Benefits from ‘Strategic Investor’ Status in Albania? (July 22, 2026)
Shaking the country
The “Flamingo Revolution” continues to shake Albania. This week, a confrontation erupted outside parliament, as demonstrators gathered to protest ahead of MPs’ final session before the summer recess.
As police sought to move demonstrators away from building, stones were thrown and water cannons deployed. Our gallery brings you the dramatic scenes from the capital, Tirana.
Read more: Albanian Protesters Clash With Police at Rally Outside Parliament (July 23, 2026)
Radical plans
Following the resignation of Prime Minister Alexandru Munteanu earlier this month, Moldova has a new government, this time led by Vasile Tofan, a former private equity firm boss.
A key element of Tofan’s programme is kickstarting economic growth by implementing tough reforms. But is Moldovan society and the ruling Action and Solidarity Party, which voted him into office, ready for the shock therapy that Tofan appears to be offering?
Read more: Financier-Turned-PM Plans Radical Cure for Moldova’s Ills (July 23, 2026)
Saving diversity
In a world where everything – including food – is widely globalised, little attention is paid to preserving the richness of local crop varieties. In one of our interviews this week, we talked to Mirjana Jankulovska from the Faculty of Agricultural Sciences and Food in Skopje, North Macedonia.
For 15 years, Jankulovska has led a team of scientists seeking to preserve rare crop varieties that have survived only in North Macedonia’s villages. Jankulovska speaks about what has been achieved so far – and what her team still hopes to achieve.
Read more: Ancient Seeds, Lost Beans: The Professor Saving North Macedonia’s Vanishing Crops (July 20, 2026)

items.title: First Freddie Mercury Bust in Hungary to Be Unveiled at Lake Balaton
items.summary: As a highlight of the Queen Festival, Hungary’s first public bust of Freddie Mercury will be unveiled on Saturday evening at the Music Pavilion in Balatonszemes, the organizers announced. The initiative is a collaboration between the Queen Friends’ Circle Cultural Association and the municipality of Balatonszemes, and the installation of the bust has been officially […] The post First Freddie Mercury Bust in Hungary to Be Unveiled at Lake Balaton appeared first on Hungary Today.
items.body_text:
At the House of Music Hungary, a large-scale exhibition explores the life and legacy of Freddie Mercury and Queen, marking 40 years since their historic Budapest concert.Continue reading
As a highlight of the Queen Festival, Hungary’s first public bust of Freddie Mercury will be unveiled on Saturday evening at the Music Pavilion in Balatonszemes, the organizers announced.
The initiative is a collaboration between the Queen Friends’ Circle Cultural Association and the municipality of Balatonszemes, and the installation of the bust has been officially approved by Sony Music’s management.
One of the event’s guests of honor will be Peter Freestone, the singer’s former personal assistant.
The press release quotes Arnold Gyarmati, president of the Queen Friends’ Circle Cultural Association, who said that the project was preceded by several years of preparatory work and numerous consultations. “We set out on this journey in 2019. We considered other locations, but ultimately the idea found a home in Balatonszemes.” The president emphasized that a major factor in the decision was the fact that the Queen community has been active in Balatonszemes for over thirty years, and that the Balatonszemes municipal government also played an important role in the memorial’s creation.
Arnold Gyarmati added that since Mayor Zsolt Iváncsics took office, progress on the statue has accelerated, and as a result of joint consultations, the unveiling is scheduled to take place at the end of July. The bust was created by sculptor András Sándor Kocsis. The organizers oversaw the entire creative process to ensure that the most authentic portrait of the singer possible was produced. According to the announcement, this will be the third public statue of Freddie Mercury in the world.
He added that the Freddie Mercury bust could also boost Balatonszemes’s international profile. “I am certain that the statue’s location will become a place of pilgrimage, and visitors from many countries around the world will come to us to visit this memorial site,” said the mayor.
The press release notes that the Queen camp in Balatonszemes began in the early 1990s and has grown into a festival over the years. This year’s event coincides with several anniversaries, as it marks both the 80th anniversary of Freddie Mercury’s birth and the 40th anniversary of the band’s concert in Budapest. The 33rd Queen Festival will be held in Balatonszemes from July 22 to 26. The program includes concerts by several tribute bands, community events, and cultural activities.
The press release also quotes Zsolt Iváncsics, mayor of Balatonszemes, who said
the Freddie Mercury bust will find a fitting home in the town, which already commemorates the legacies of actors Zoltán Latinovits and István Bujtor, illustrator Károly Reich, and writer Géza Gárdonyi.
The unveiling of the Freddie Mercury bust will take place on Saturday, July 25, at 7:00 p.m. at the Music Pavilion, followed by a laser show and concerts for attendees. All festival events are free to attend.
Via MTI, Featured image: Pixabay (illustration)

items.title: Medieval Festival in Szeged Celebrates John Hunyadi’s Victory at Belgrade
items.summary: Statue of John Hunyadi (Hungarian: Hunyadi János) in Pécs A medieval festival will be held on Saturday beside the Franciscan Church in Szeged, where cultural programs, medieval weapons and combat demonstrations, traditional dances, and children’s activities will commemorate the 570th anniversary of the Siege of Belgrade, the organizers announced. The event was launched in 2006, […] The post Medieval Festival in Szeged Celebrates John Hunyadi’s Victory at Belgrade appeared first on Hungary Today.
items.body_text:
Among the highlights are artifacts from the largest known Scythian cemetery between the Danube and Tisza rivers.Continue reading
A medieval festival will be held on Saturday beside the Franciscan Church in Szeged, where cultural programs, medieval weapons and combat demonstrations, traditional dances, and children’s activities will commemorate the 570th anniversary of the Siege of Belgrade, the organizers announced.
The event was launched in 2006, on the 550th anniversary of the Siege of Belgrade, by staff members of the cultural center of the Franciscan monastery in Szeged’s Lower Town. Their aim was to create a celebration honoring John Hunyadi’s victory over the Ottomans and, alongside the many national days of mourning, to also pay tribute to Hungary’s great historic victories.
In the summer of 1456, the crusaders led by Saint John of Capistrano stopped near the Franciscan monastery in Szeged, at what is now Mátyás Square, on their way south.
The location therefore has a direct connection to the historic events commemorated by the ‘Belgrade Victory Days.’
Participants of Szeged’s only cultural program dedicated to reviving medieval traditions, which has now been held for more than two decades, will gather on Saturday morning at Klauzál Square in the city center. The lively procession, featuring musicians, drummers, and flag bearers, will then make its way to the Franciscan Church and monastery in the Lower Town, where visitors will be able to enjoy live role-playing, a children’s knight tournament, the interactive “Dragon Trail” game, a knight-themed craft workshop, and a falconry demonstration.
Visitors will be able to admire costumes and weapons at close range and experience what life was like in the military camps of King Matthias Corvinus’s famous Black Army.
Alongside martial arts displays, knightly duels, and demonstrations of medieval weapons and warfare, members of historical reenactment groups will organize dance events and concerts. Thanks to the Historical Society of Marót, visitors will also learn what firearms were used during the Ottoman period.
The program will conclude after sunset, with a fire show and fire duel by the St. Longinus Historical Society instead of fireworks. The following morning, a ceremonial mass will be held at the Franciscan Church in honor of the 570th anniversary of the Siege of Belgrade.
The Christian Hungarian forces led by John Hunyadi inflicted a crushing defeat on the army of Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II on July 22, 1456. In 2011, the Hungarian Parliament declared the date a national day of remembrance for the Siege of Belgrade.
Via MTI, Featured image: MTI/Ruprech Judit

items.title: Hungarian Autonomy Efforts in the Carpathian Basin Take Center Stage at Tusnádfürdő
items.summary: Young Hungarian participants arrive at the Bálványos Summer University During the panel discussion on efforts toward Hungarian autonomy in the Carpathian Basin, which took place on Thursday as part of the Bálványos Summer University (“Tusványos”) in Băile Tușnad (Tusnádfürdő, Romania), the participants emphasized the importance of EU regulations, the collective will, and the stance of […] The post Hungarian Autonomy Efforts in the Carpathian Basin Take Center Stage at Tusnádfürdő appeared first
items.body_text:
The protesters handed over a petition to the representative of the Romanian government.Continue reading
During the panel discussion on efforts toward Hungarian autonomy in the Carpathian Basin, which took place on Thursday as part of the Bálványos Summer University (“Tusványos”) in Băile Tușnad (Tusnádfürdő, Romania), the participants emphasized the importance of EU regulations, the collective will, and the stance of the majority.
Katalin Szili, former Speaker of Parliament, stressed that autonomy is not an end in itself but a means to ensure the continued existence of Hungarian communities in neighboring countries. In her view, the most effective way to achieve this would be through international assistance,
if the European Union were to require member states to recognize indigenous minorities as a state-forming factor.
Elvira Kovács, vice president of the Serbian National Assembly and a member of the executive board of the Alliance of Vojvodina Hungarians (VMSZ), emphasized the importance of a unified approach by the minority community for the majority to accept autonomy.
She recalled that the creation of the legal framework for the Hungarian National Council, which enshrines the community’s cultural autonomy in Serbia, was preceded by a long process—beginning with the community initiative launched during the Yugoslav Wars, through the 2002 Law on the Protection of Rights and Freedoms of National Minorities and Serbia’s 2006 Constitution, which recognizes minorities as state-forming factors with collective rights, all the way to the election of the National Councils in 2010.
The politician noted that
since Serbia is still awaiting accession, pressure from the European Union has also helped the national communities
and, for example, forced Belgrade to adopt an action plan for minorities.
Former Liberal Education Minister Gábor Fodor also pointed out that the EU accession process has brought about progress in the area of minority rights in numerous Central and Eastern European countries, at least compared to the era of communist dictatorships. To successfully resolve the legal disputes with Brussels, one must understand that
the Union views minorities with concern because it fears secession.
On the other hand, based on the examples of the Baltic states and Ukraine, it fears that Russia could use internal ethnic tensions as a pretext for intervention.
According to Fodor, a country’s stance toward minorities is an indispensable factor in advancing Hungarian autonomy efforts in the Carpathian Basin, and this can be greatly influenced by whether the community’s representatives are part of the government.
Dávid Sobor, the legal representative of the Szekler National Council (SZNT), which has made the territorial autonomy of Szeklerland its main objective, spoke about the European Citizens’ Initiative on national regions, which aims for a fairer distribution of cohesion funds and the prevention of discrimination against national regions.
According to moderator György Csóti’s conclusion, the success of the struggle for autonomy depends on the community’s resolute will, the legal system of the respective country, and international conditions that make it possible to exert external pressure.
Via MTI; Featured photo: MTI/Veres Nándor

items.title: Augusztus 1-től még könnyebb lesz éjszaka kijutni Budapest agglomerációjába
items.summary: Több új járat is indul, amik az utolsó metrókhoz, HÉV-ekhez és vonatokhoz is igazodnak.
items.body_text:
Augusztus 1-től még könnyebb lesz éjszaka kijutni Budapest agglomerációjába
Augusztus 1-jétől tovább bővül az éjszakai agglomerációs közlekedés, Budapestről még több település irányába lesz könnyebb az eljutás – írja az MTI Vitézy Dávid közlekedési és beruházási miniszter Facebook-posztja alapján. Bejegyzésében azt írta, hogy a járatokat az utolsó metrókhoz és a HÉV-ek, illetve vonatok menetrendjéhez igazítják.
Közvetlen éjszakai kapcsolat jön létre Budapest és Biatorbágy térsége között. Az éjszakai járatok Kelenföldről indulnak, és Biatorbágy után érintik Sóskutat, Pusztazámort és Etyeket. Szigethalomra, Halásztelekre és Tökölre augusztus 11-étől indulnak az éjszakai buszok Kelenföldről, az M4-es metrótól csatlakozva.
Solymárról is több település válik könnyebben elérhetővé augusztustól, és szintén újdonság, hogy néhány nap múlva Újpest Városkaputól egészen Visegrádig lehet majd utazni éjszakánként.
Az utolsó H5-ös HÉV-től is bővítik a csatlakozásokat; Pomáztól Pilisszentkereszt és Csobánka felé is új járat indul. Veresegyház környékének elérése is egyszerűbbé válik éjszaka, a Stadion állomástól indulnak új járatok, amik mind érintik Szadát, Erdőkertest, Őrbottyánt és Csomádot is. Csömörre és Nagytarcsára való eljutás is egyszerűbbé válik, a járatok az Örs vezér térről indulnak majd.
Az éjszakai agglomerációs közlekedés bővítésének köszönhetően egészen Dabasig lehet utazni augusztustól, és közvetlen éjszakai kapcsolat jön létre Budapest és Kiskunlacháza térsége között is. A Budapest-Belgrád vasútvonal megnyitásáig a Dunaharaszti-Taksony-Dunavarsány-Délegyháza útvonalon haladva Kiskunlacháza után még Dömsöd is elérhető válik. A 150-es vasútvonal elindulását követően pedig a busz Taksony-Dunavarsány-Délegyháza helyett Bugyi érintésével közlekedik majd.

items.title: Jön a következő God of War Kratosszal, kapcsolódni fog Laufey sztorijához
items.summary: Kratos feleségének játéka a tervek szerint februárban érkezik.
items.body_text:
Jön a következő God of War Kratosszal, kapcsolódni fog Laufey sztorijához
A Santa Monica Studio már dolgozik a következő God of War játékon, aminek főszereplője ismét Kratos lesz – írja az IGN. A stúdió ezt a San Diego Comic Conon jelentette be, ahogy azt is, hogy az új játék története szorosan kapcsolódik majd a God of War Laufey-éhoz, aminek Kratos halott felesége, Faye a főszereplője. Ez a játék, ha minden jól megy, február 16-án jelenik majd meg.
Ezen kívül semmit nem osztottak meg a még készülő Kratos-játékról. Nem tudni, hogy mikor jön, milyen platformra, de még a címe sem derült ki. Cory Barlog, a stúdió vezetője a Laufey-ről azt mondta, hogy ki akarták tágítani a God of War világát, hogy olyan karakterek is megjelenjenek, akikre a játékosok nem számítanak.
A Laufey fogadtatása nem volt osztatlan siker, de Barlog júniusban megígérte, hogy amíg a sorozat folytatódik, mindig lesz God of War, aminek Kratos a főszereplője. Ezt a Santa Monica Studio hivatalos posztban is megerősítette.

items.summary: Giorgi Akhobadze, a doctor and anti-government activist, has been sentenced to 25 days of administrative detention after Tbilisi City Court Judge Manuchar Tsatsua reportedly found him guilty of several administrative offenses stemming from allegedly insulting public and police officials, including on social media. items.body_text:
Activist Giorgi Akhobadze Jailed for 25 Days Over ‘Insulting’ Officials
Giorgi Akhobadze, a doctor and anti-government activist, has been sentenced to 25 days of administrative detention after Tbilisi City Court Judge Manuchar Tsatsua reportedly found him guilty of several administrative offenses stemming from allegedly insulting public and police officials, including on social media.
Several media outlets reported that the proceedings consolidated a series of administrative cases, including Facebook posts where Akhobadze allegedly insulted Georgian Dream Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, GD lawmaker Levan Makhashvili, and police officer Grigol Kachkachishvili.
Kachkachishvili, an investigator, was involved in the earlier criminal case against Akhobadze, who spent eight months in pre-trial custody on serious drug charges. Akhobadze’s verdict in August 2025 marked the first not-guilty verdict in a series of arrests and prosecutions that government critics linked with pro-EU protests that erupted in November 2024. Similar drug-related arrests sparked allegations that police may be planting drugs against government critics.
“F**k every police officer who plants drugs. I will repeat myself here again,” Akhobadze told TV Pirveli, reacting to the July 24 ruling, noting he had also used the phrase during an earlier phone conversation with Kachkachishvili while trying to recover the items confiscated when he was detained on drug charges.
The administrative detention follows another administrative case against Akhobadze earlier this month. On July 8, the Tbilisi City Court fined him GEL 3,000 (about USD 1,140) over a Facebook comment directed at Vato Shakarashvili, a member of the anti-EU and Georgian Dream-aligned group United Neutral Georgia. Akhobadze’s refusal to pay that fine allegedly contributed to a stricter penalty.
The ruling also came two days after a similar ruling sentencing Formula TV journalist Vakho Sanaia to two weeks’ detention over a Facebook post about Georgian Dream MPs, a decision that drew widespread condemnation, including from foreign officials and international human rights groups.
Expanding Crackdown
Akhobadze’s latest detention comes amid an expanding crackdown on social media posts deemed “insulting” toward public officials and figures.
Although a series of rulings over public “insults” had been delivered over the past year, with the ruling Georgian Dream party pledging last summer to proactively sue critics over social media “insults,” the crackdown intensified after the Interior Ministry’s Division for Combating Hate Speech started its work on June 1, 2026. The division’s stated goal is to proactively monitor what authorities describe as “hate speech” in public spaces, including on social media, and to submit administrative complaints to the courts.
Since its launch, the division has initiated dozens of administrative cases over social media posts and comments, resulting in fines ranging from GEL 1,500 to GEL 6,000. Hearings related to these cases have become a regular feature in courts across the country.
Most of the proceedings rely on Articles 166 (petty hooliganism) and 173 (insulting or disobeying a police officer) of Georgia’s Code of Administrative Offenses.
The division’s work has drawn criticism from opposition politicians and government critics, who argue that sanctions have been imposed even when the public officials allegedly “insulted” neither filed complaints nor were asked whether they considered the statements offensive. Critics have also pointed to the broad interpretation adopted by the courts, saying that findings of “insult” have extended beyond swearing, including to curses.
