National Bank Says EU-Sanctioned Georgia-Based Crypto Firms Not Under Its Regulation
The National Bank of Georgia (NBG) said that three Georgia-based crypto-related service platforms included in the EU’s latest sanctions package against Russia are not under its regulation.
In a statement issued on July 24, the NBG identified the sanctioned companies as Aifory LLC, Abcex LLC, and Rapira Group LLC, stressing that “none of their areas of activity was Georgia” and that “investigative actions have been launched against them.”
The names of two companies identified by the NBG — Aifory LLC and Rapira Group LLC — match those of entities sanctioned by the United Kingdom in May over “Russia-focused exchanges seeking to evade sanctions.”
The European Union unveiled its 21st round of sanctions against Russia on July 23, conditionally including the Kulevi oil refinery on Georgia’s Black Sea coast, with a transaction ban due to take effect in six months unless the decision is reviewed. The package also targeted 14 crypto-related service platforms based in Georgia, Panama, the UAE, the Marshall Islands, Kyrgyzstan, and Belarus.
Georgia’s Foreign Ministry issued a statement on Kulevi’s conditional inclusion on the sanctions list, saying there were “no factual or legal grounds” for the move and expressing hope that the bloc would review the decision before it takes effect in January 2027.

items.body_text:
Russian Money Transfer System Zolotaya Korona Halts Transfers to Georgia Following EU Sanctions
Russia’s Zolotaya Korona money transfer system has stopped allowing transfers to Georgia following the European Union’s latest sanctions package against Moscow, Russian media have reported.
Georgia no longer appears on the list of countries available for transfers through the service, while transfers to several other unspecified countries have also reportedly been suspended.
The EU announced its 21st package of sanctions against Russia on 23 July. The measures reportedly target, among others, the operator of Zolotaya Korona, the Novosibirsk-based Payment Center.
According to reports, Zolotaya Korona is one of Russia’s major money transfer systems, having become a key channel for international transfers after Visa and Mastercard suspended operations in the country following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The latest sanctions package also conditionally included Georgia’s Kulevi oil refinery, with a transaction ban set to take effect in six months unless the decision is reviewed. The package additionally targeted cryptocurrency-related service platforms in Georgia and several other countries.

items.title: Aliyev greenlights ‘involuntary psychiatric hospitalisation’ law
items.summary: The amendments would allow authorities to refer people for psychiatric evaluation without their consent.
items.body_text:
Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev has approved legislative amendments allowing the authorities to refer people for psychiatric evaluations without their consent. Critics warn that the amendments could allow the authorities to ‘involuntarily hospitalise’ and silence government critics.
The changes came as amendments to the law on psychiatric care, which Aliyev approved on Thursday.
According to the law, prosecutors can refer people subjected to administrative proceedings if delays in providing psychiatric core pose a ‘threat to that person’s life or health, or the life or health of others.
Human rights defender Yalchin Imanov told OC Media that the law in question already provides for a system of involuntary hospitalisation.
He noted that under current legislation, a person can be committed to a psychiatric facility ‘only if specific grounds exist and based on a psychiatrist’s assessment and a court order’.
‘The law states that even if a person with a severe mental disorder or illness has not committed a crime, they can — given specific grounds — be placed in a psychiatric facility for examination and treatment by court order, against their will’, Imanov said.
He emphasised that the law takes into account the immediate danger an individual poses to themself or others, ‘the inability to meet basic life needs independently due to a mental disorder’, and the risk of irreparable harm to health if medical care is not provided.
In his view, the main problem lies in the fact that the concept of ‘danger’ and the criteria for defining a mental disorder are not clearly defined in the legislation:
‘The legislation does not establish specific criteria or indicators for this. It merely states that a person with a mental disorder must pose an immediate danger to themselves or others. This is vague wording. Such ambiguity can create fertile ground for abuse by the Azerbaijani authorities’, Imanov stressed.
Imanov believes that ‘this ambiguity poses a particular risk to political activists and critics of the government’.
He highlighted that experience shows that such vague wording creates a risk of abuse and the involuntary hospitalisation of political activists, especially those who criticise the authorities:
‘Such incidents have occurred before, and there is no guarantee they won’t happen again’, Imanov said.
He cited the case of the opposition Popular Front Party member Agil Humbatov as an example.
Humbatov was forcibly committed to the Republican Psychiatric Hospital in April 2020 after criticising the government’s policies during the pandemic.
‘It was reported that some medicines of unknown origin were used on him without his consent or that of his relatives’, Imanov said, adding that the government could use this mechanism against its critics.
‘Given the Azerbaijani government’s extreme intolerance of political freedoms, it is hardly surprising that it resorts to the tactic of committing political critics and opponents to psychiatric institutions’.

items.title: Armenia grants state-owned property to media outlet owned by pro-Western party leader
items.summary: The decision has raised concerns among media experts.
items.body_text:
The Armenian government has granted the operator of the news website 1in.am the right to use state-owned property in central Yerevan free of charge for three years. The decision has prompted criticism from media experts, who cited the lack of transparent criteria for providing state support to individual media outlets.
The decision was approved at the government’s 23 July session.
Under the decision, Sksizb Media Centre LLC, which operates 1in.am, will receive a 250-square-metre space in central Yerevan.
According to the government’s justification, the State Property Management Committee received an application from 1in.am requesting that the premises be ‘provided to the company free of charge to ensure the continuation of its regular and uninterrupted operations’.
The company also submitted an investment programme under which it pledged to invest ֏10 million ($26,000) over the next two years. The funds are to be used to renovate the premises, furnish workspaces, modernise technical infrastructure, and improve conditions for producing news content.
The proposal also envisages the production of at least 14,000 videos, reports, interviews, or programmes over three years, while generating at least 54 million views or reads across the outlet’s website and social media platforms.
Sksizb Media Centre was established in 2006 and it launched 1in.am in 2010. The company is owned by Arman Babajanyan, the leader of the Rally For the Republic party, who headed the party’s list in Armenia’s June 2026 parliamentary elections, but fell short of the threshold to join parliament.
He previously entered parliament in 2018 on the list of the Bright Armenia party before leaving its parliamentary faction the following year to serve as an independent MP. He founded the Rally For the Republic party in 2021 and has since become one of Armenia’s most prominent pro-Western politicians.
The party advocates closer ties with the EU, Armenia’s withdrawal from the Russian-led Collective Security Treaty Organisation (CSTO) and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), the normalisation of relations with neighbouring countries, and what it describes as ‘horizontal’ relations with Russia.
Babajanyan has also campaigned for Armenia’s European integration, including through the Eurovote initiative, as a result of which a bill calls on the government to seek EU integration in its second and final hearing submitted to the parliament and was eventually adopted in March 2025.
In an editorial statement published on Friday, 1in.am said the outlet had recently been facing financial and organisational difficulties due to rising rental costs.
The outlet said this prompted it to ask the government to consider allocating state-owned premises free of charge and expressed gratitude for its positive decision.
‘This decision will allow us to direct our limited resources towards the development of the news outlet, upgrading our technical capabilities, implementing new projects, and producing higher-quality journalism’, the statement read.
The decision has drawn criticism from media experts, who told CivilNet such state support for an individual media outlet is ‘problematic’, and stressed the importance of it being provided transparently and according to pre-established criteria.

items.title: 3 reasons why your electric bill may be rising
items.summary: Low water levels in the Nordic countries, turmoil in the Middle East and a corporate takeover may all impact electricity costs in the coming months.
items.body_text:
There is more upward pressure than usual on electricity prices next winter, experts say. That's due to low hydropower production in Sweden and Norway and the Iran war, which is raising electricity prices across Europe.
"Water reserves have dropped in the Nordic countries. This affects the price of electricity, especially at times when we have little wind power production or the weather is particularly cold," explains Pekka Salomaa, director of the Finnish Energy industry group.
Military operations in the Persian Gulf region are also reducing the availability of natural gas, which still used to produce a significant portion of Central Europe's electricity. That has knock-on effects in the Nordic region as well, he says.
Meanwhile, electricity transfer fees may rise in some parts of Finland due to a buyout of the electricity distribution company Caruna.
The new owner, Spanish energy giant Iberdrola, could hike those fees, Pertti Järventausta, Tampere University professor of electrical engineering said on Yle's A-studio this week.
In late 2023, Finland's Energy Authority introduced a new regulatory model that allows electricity distribution companies to raise transfer fees.
Any price increase is most likely to affect customers in southwestern and northeastern Finland.
Iberdrola announced on Tuesday that it plans to buy Caruna. The deal is worth around two billion euros, but still requires approval from EU authorities.

items.title: Finnish MP vows to stay in Parliament despite final conviction on assault and weapons charges
items.summary: The Supreme Court left in place former Finns Party MP Timo Vornanen's convictions related to a drunken late-night shooting incident at a Helsinki karaoke bar.
items.body_text:
The Finnish Supreme Court has declined to reconsider the legal case of independent MP Timo Vornanen. He sought to appeal his conviction on an array of offences related to a shooting incident in downtown Helsinki in April 2024.
Last December, the former Finns Party MP was previously found guilty by the Helsinki District Court on charges of assault, unlawful threats and several firearms offences.
Vornanen was sentenced to eight months' suspended prison sentence. With his bid to appeal rejected, that verdict is now final and legally binding.
"I find this decision regrettable from the perspective of people's legal protection," Vornanen wrote in a social media post on Friday.
"I will now focus on my duties as an MP"
Vornanen, a former police officer, previously said that he would consider resigning from his parliamentary seat if he was ultimately convicted of the offences.
However Vornanen indicated on Friday that he intends to remain in Parliament despite the final verdict.
"I will now focus on fulfilling my duties as an MP and continue my work for the benefit of the Finns," Vornanen wrote. Parliamentary elections will be held next spring.
Due to the incident, Vornanen was expelled from the Finns Party parliamentary group in May 2024. Since then, he has served in the legislature as a one-man parliamentary group.
Yle was unable to reach Vornanen for comment on Friday.

items.title: Finnish spy agency issues new warning of Russian cyberattacks – this time via email servers
items.summary: Laundry Bear poses a serious cyber espionage threat to organisations in public administration, critical infrastructure and the defence sector, says Supo.
items.body_text:
The Finnish Security and Intelligence Service (Supo) has issued several warnings recently about cyber espionage efforts directed at Finland by Russia and other authoritarian states.
On Friday, Supo teamed up with the Finnish Defence Intelligence Agency and the US National Security Agency (NSA) to issue an advisory about a Russian state-sponsored cyber threat actor that targets organisational email systems.
Earlier this month, Supo warned Finnish firms about a Russian cyber-espionage campaign targeting vulnerable network devices.
"Serious cyber espionage threat" from Laundry Bear
On Friday, intelligence authorities said that companies and organisations should be aware of a lesser-known Russian cyber threat actor known as Laundry Bear.
Authorities said that Laundry Bear poses a serious cyber espionage threat especially to organisations in public administration, critical infrastructure and the defence sector.
Laundry Bear has targeted a wide range of victims, including military industry operators, state administration and other authorities, technology companies and third sector operators, Supo said in a statement.
Russian human intelligence weakened since 2022
Its main targets have been Nato countries – including Finland – as well as Ukraine.
"Laundry Bear has primarily attempted to break into the email systems of the targeted organisation, often using simple but effective methods such as social manipulation (e.g. impersonation) and stolen user IDs," Supo explained.
Russian human intelligence efforts in the West have been undercut by the expulsions of Russian intelligence officers since Moscow's invasion of Ukraine nearly four and a half years ago.
As a result, Russia has been forced to increasingly resort to cyber methods in its espionage activity, the spy agency said.

items.title: An essential guide to travelling through Copenhagen Airport with kids
items.summary: Flying with children can be stressful at the best of times, so here are The Local’s best tips for departing from Copenhagen Airport with your kids in tow.
items.body_text:
Things to do
Obviously, your family’s needs will vary depending on the age of your children. If you have young children, it can be a good idea for them to blow off some steam before getting on the flight.
A great way to do this can be to head to one of the airport’s playgrounds. There’s one after security near the entrance to Finger B, complete with luggage carts, a control tower with a slide, and a couple of planes for kids to climb on.
There’s also an outdoor playground before security with a couple of slides hidden inside a wooden cloud, outside Terminal 2.
Make sure to check out the large blue fish tank before security, too. It’s just next to Lagkagehuset/Ole and Steen and WOK restaurant near the baggage drop in Terminal 2.
There are also two Lego shops inside the airport: one between gates A&B and one between gates B&C. These are both after security.
If you want to buy something to keep your slightly older child occupied during the flight, there are a number of 7-Elevens which sell magazines, sticker and activity books and stationery, as well as snacks and drinks. Look for the 7-Eleven Read and Fly signs.
There’s also a child area in the SAS lounge with toys and children’s TV – free for SAS Business or Plus travellers or Gold EuroBonus members.
For non-members, entry costs around 300 Danish kroner per person, with free entry for kids under 2. You have to be flying with a Sky Team airline. Entry is sometimes cheaper off-season and you may be able to pay with EuroBonus reward points if you’ve got a stash saved up.
The SAS lounge also includes a buffet with unlimited drinks (including alcohol, which is maybe less relevant if you're travelling with kids), as well as wifi, newspapers and magazines included in your entry fee. If you were planning on grabbing a meal, drinks and perhaps a coffee in the airport anyway it can often work out the same or cheaper, especially as the lounge offers unlimited hot drinks (even quite fancy ones made by actual baristas) and pastries.
There are other lounges at Copenhagen ‒ the Aspire lounge, Danske Bank Aviator Business Lounge, Carlsberg Aviator lounge and Eventyr lounge. Of these, the only other one with a designated kids area is the Eventyr lounge, at the top of gate C after passport control, which means you can only access it if your flight is leaving from that gate (some but not all flights leaving Schengen).
Entry for the Eventyr lounge also costs around 300 Danish kroner per person (free for kids under 2). Again, it's only open to people travelling on certain airlines or who have certain cards or memberships, so make sure to check you qualify before you travel.
As an aside, it's worth noting that transiting, arriving and departing passengers all share the same space at Copenhagen Airport (once they are on the gate side of security). So the same areas that can be used by families before departing are also available to anyone transiting through Copenhagen and you can also use them on arrival if you somehow have the energy for this.
Getting through security
Just before you get to the actual queues for security, there will be a child-size security scanner made out of Lego. If your child is scared about flying or worried about going through security, you can act out the process here to make them feel less nervous.
If you have kids under six, you’ll be sent to the family lane at security, with another security officer made out of Lego pointing the way.
If your child uses a buggy (stroller), you may need to check it in depending on size. Usually if it’s a small buggy you can fold down (a klapvogn or paraplyvogn in Danish), you can take it through security all the way to your gate. If it’s larger, you’ll probably have to check it in at the baggage drop and borrow an airport buggy after security.

items.title: Swedish migration minister: 'One day you're a Nazi, the next a left-wing activist'
items.summary: Swedish Migration Minister Johan Forssell speaks to The Local's Richard Orange about the personal attacks he's received in his role, and why he thinks immigration will play a significant role in the upcoming election.
items.body_text:
Whatever you think about the citizenship, asylum and work permit reforms driven through by Johan Forssell, few would dispute that he has been one of Sweden’s hardest-working ministers. When The Local meets Sweden's migration minister at the Almedalen political festival on Gotland, he's looking more relaxed than he has in recent months.
"This spring has been extremely intensive and still is intensive," he says over coffee and cinnamon rolls served in a ruined medieval building. "I think I've had 12 bills this spring, and on top of that we've had a breakdown in the parliamentary pairing system, so it hasn't exactly been easy. But we're pretty much there with most of it now."
He estimates that just two ministers – Justice Minister Gunnar Strömmer and himself – have been responsible for over 60 percent of the Tidö Agreement, the political programme the government agreed in October 2022 with the far-right Sweden Democrats. And because the government did everything by the book – with inquiries appointed and their conclusions sent out to consultation before bills are drafted – all the work hit his ministry at around the same time.
"There's been a high tempo. It's not like people should feel sorry for us, but the effort put in at the ministry has been immense because it's not just been delivering on the Tidö Agreement, which anyway involved historic changes, we have also had the issue of the deportation of certain young people which we have worked intensively to find a solution to."
The biggest problem faced by the Justice Ministry, which includes the Migration Ministry, has not, he adds, been dealing with the far-right Sweden Democrats, as many assume, but instead simply finding enough qualified judges and lawyers to hold inquiries and draw up all this new legislation.
On top of the workload, he's also had to deal with the personal attacks that come with the role of migration minister, something he did not experience in his previous roles as minister for trade and aid, or as chief of staff of Sweden's last Moderate Party prime minister, Fredrik Reinfeldt.
"I've worked on several different issues in my time as a politician, and this one is bloody well not easy, I have to say that," he continues. "You have to put up with so many things and so many abusive remarks: one day you're a Nazi, the next a left-wing activist. You get it from both sides."
When The Local asks how he has handled the pressure personally, he falls back on the words from the famous British Second World War motivational poster: "Keep calm and carry on!"
Forssell says he is proud of the laws that he has driven through, particularly on citizenship, even if a scandal over the parliamentary pairing system hogged the headlines.
As The Local was first to report, the Sweden Democrats sent in two MPs to vote who they had promised to hold back under the Swedish parliament's pairing agreement, allowing the government to defeat an opposition motion to add transitional provisions to the citizenship law.
This means that more than 100,000 people who had already applied for citizenship are now having their cases decided on the basis of rules that were not in place when they applied, in many cases several years ago.
The opposition parties have also declared the pairing agreement broken, arguing that the Sweden Democrats can no longer be trusted, after cheated to defeat the vote. This means that for the rest of this parliamentary term, all MPs will have to be physically present in parliament to have their vote counted.
"That shouldn't distract from the big picture, which is that we finally have a legal framework that is in line with what's in place in the rest of Europe: a language requirement, civics test, and a self-sufficiency requirement. These are all things Sweden has not had for 50 years."

items.title: Inside Germany: A punk rock protest, festival season and immigrant music
items.summary: From the group of punks that invades Germany's bougiest island every summer to the Iranian artist rapping about her passport struggles, Inside Germany is our weekly look at some of the recent news and talking points that you may have missed.
items.body_text:
In Germany, life falls into a seasonal rhythm.
The autumn is marked by beer fests, cooler weather and vibrant foliage. Then comes the winter, a time for reflection – ideally alongside a good friend in a hot sauna. The spring brings a sense of rejuvenation, and excitement for the travel you have planned and the summer season to come.
And now it's July, so naturally the punks have taken Sylt again!
This year's month long, and legally permitted, protest marks the fifth summer in a row that a punk occupation has taken place on Germany's infamously posh summer vacation destination.
In case you missed it, the now annual punk takeover of Sylt can be traced back to at least 2022, and seems to have started organically.
That year saw the introduction of the 9-euro ticket (the first iteration of what is now the Deutschlandticket), which led to a sort-of joke that Germany's poor, left-leaning city folk would head north and fill up the country's pristine beaches. The joke grew into a viral meme, and then an actual movement. Ironically, the whole thing may have been sparked by an article in Bild which worried about exactly that.
READ ALSO: Punks take over posh German island to take on the far right
Long known as a summer play place for Germany's rich and famous, Sylt has been home to a fair share of controversies. Such as in 2024 when a video of young people shouting Nazi slogans to the tune of a popular song went viral.
The punk protest here can be seen as standing against conservative and far-right politics, and drawing attention to the social injustice that wealthy people can afford to holiday in Germany's nicest locations while lower income taxpayers generally cannot.
The district of North Frisia had tried to stop the protest this year, but an administrative court ruled in favour of the protesters, saying it was protected freedom of expression.
The initiative "Action Sylt" which organises the protest, pays fees for utilities to the district while the camp is established.
Where is this?
Festival season is in full swing in Germany now.
Just this weekend, festival seekers could choose between; electronic music at Open Beatz Festival in Herzogenaurach, darkwave and gothic music at Amphi Festival in Cologne, or classical and opera at the Bayreuth Festival.
Of course, reading this on Saturday, it'll be a tad late to get into those (with the exception of the Bayreuth Festival which continues through most of August).
But, if you're interested, there are plenty more festivals to choose from in the coming weeks. We detailed a few of them in our August events roundup, which you can read here.
The above photo was taken as Das Fest, a favourite summer-time event in Karlsruhe.
A theme song for the immigration office
"Got an appointment, for an appointment, for an appointment for next year..." sings Faravaz in her recently released song "Passport".
Being "stuck in the middle between Berlin and Tehran", Faravaz Farvardin has probably seen immigration challenges on a level that those of us coming from the United States or the United Kingdom can't imagine.
Still, that above lyric is bound to strike a nerve with just about every non-EU immigrant in Germany, regardless of their country of origin.
@faravaz I am still a refugee ?
♬ original sound - FARAVAZ
If you can't play the video embedded above, you can see the clip here on TikTok here or listen to the full song on Youtube.
For now, Faravaz is a little-known artist in Germany. But she joins a long list of immigrant artists to jump into the country's music scene - some of which have found tremendous success.
Starting with music from the 'Guest Worker' generation, immigrants have noticeably influenced German music since at least the 1960s.
Then in the 1990s, in response to a rising anti-immigrant and xenophobic sentiment, second generation Turkish-German artists contributed to the booming German hip-hop scene. This continued to develop until today, and led to the rise of some of the biggest artists in rece

items.title: Can you really be fined for killing wasps in Germany?
items.summary: Wasps in Germany are protected by the country's Federal Nature Conservation Act. Here's why you shouldn't go around killing them.
items.body_text:
It wouldn’t be summer in Germany without wasps. Anyone who sets up a picnic in the park, or even a barbecue on their balcony in the summer months here is bound to deal with at least a couple.
The wasps you will most often find in Germany are the “common wasp” and the “German wasp”. They aren’t really dangerous, except to people with wasp allergies.
These two species have a very similar appearance, and can be equally annoying due to their taste for sweet drinks, fruits and even meats.
But while a couple hungry wasps can be quite obnoxious, you would be advised not to try and squash them.
In fact, should you succeed in killing a wasp, you could technically be forced to pay thousands of euros in fines, according to German law.
Can I really be fined for killing a wasp?
The short answer is: yes.
Wildlife in Germany is generally protected by the Federal Nature Conservation Act (Bundesnaturschutzgesetz).
Wasps in particular are mentioned in the conservation act, and are protected from “capture, injury or death without reasonable cause”.
Recommended fines for killing wasps vary from state to state, but they start around €5,000 and can go as high as €50,000.
That said, this fine is rarely enforced. It generally exists as a deterrence measure, and there are a couple important exceptions.
A German lawyer who specialises in animal law, Andreas Ackenheil, told Euronews that people who are allergic to wasp stings could be allowed to kill a wasp if they were being threatened.
Additionally, problem wasp nests can be removed, but a permit is required.
Therefore if you find a wasp nest on your home, you’re better off calling a pest control service, which would have the necessary permit to handle the removal.
Plenty of other wild animals enjoy similar protections to wasps in Germany including beetles, bumblebees and butterflies as well as squirrels, moles and wolves, for example.
So generally speaking, killing wildlife in Germany is not advisable.
READ ALSO: How to deal with fruit flies (and other critters) plaguing your German flat
How to deal with wasps legally
One German phrase about wasps is quite telling. It goes: Töte einen und es werden fünf an der Beerdigung teilnehmen (Kill one and five will attend the funeral).
There is some scientific truth to this idiom. It’s been observed that a wasp in distress can send a pheromone signal that attracts other wasps, as if it is calling for backup.
So rather than killing a wasp, or violently chasing it away, the best advice for dealing with wasps is to keep calm and avoid swatting at it directly.
Wasps are attracted to scents – namely food smells – so good hygiene measures like keeping foods sealed and not letting food covered garbage pile up are among the best preventions.
Keeping drinks covered also helps.
Wasps’ sensitivity to scent can also be used against them. Place some cloves in a lemon wedge, or burn some coffee grounds to deter them.
If all else fails, a small offering can distract a couple wasps and keep them busy elsewhere while you’re eating. A dab of jam or a bit overripe fruit left a few metres from your picnic table should do the trick.
The wasps may still check out your spread, but after being shooed away a couple times, they’ll likely figure it out.
About wasps in Germany
Wasps (Wespen in German) are also called yellowjackets or hornets and are closely related to bees and ants. They live in family groups in a nest with an egg-laying queen and a group of non-reproducing workers.
According to the environmental organisation BUND, there are around 630 unique wasp species in Germany.
Wasps play important roles in their local ecosystems as both predators and prey.
A small wasp colony can eat up to 3,000 other insect pests per day in the form of flies, mosquitoes, etc.
They are also useful as pollinators for some flowering plants.

items.title: How many newly naturalised Germans have their citizenship revoked each year?
items.summary: German citizenship can only be revoked in very specific situations, but the number of revocations jumped significantly last year compared to recent years.
items.body_text:
According to Germany's Basic Law German citizenship cannot be revoked in most cases. But exceptions apply, in specific cases, so long as the loss of citizenship does not result in the affected person becoming stateless.
What this means in practical terms is that those people born German citizens, who are not dual citizens, cannot lose their citizenship. Whereas dual-citizens, including foreigners who naturalise as German, can have their citizenship revoked by German authorities -- although only in a few situations that are specifically defined by the Nationality Act.
For example, German citizenship can be revoked from people who join the armed forces of another nation without the consent of the German authorities.
The much more common reason a newly naturalised German would see their citizenship revoked, however, is for having lied on their citizenship application.
As a spokesperson for the Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI) told The Local, "An unlawful naturalisation can be revoked within ten years of its [being granted]...if it was obtained through fraudulent misrepresentation, duress, or bribery, or through intentionally false or incomplete information that was material to the authority's decision."
READ ALSO: When can your German citizenship be revoked?
How many people are losing their German citizenship each year?
Asked how many people have seen their German citizenship revoked in recent years, the Interior Ministry provided the following numbers:
- 64 in the year 2020
- 135 in the year 2021
- 134 in the year 2022
- 174 in the year 2023
- 233 in the year 2024
- 481 in the year 2025
- 5 (as of January 19th) in 2026
The BMI spokesperson noted that the "reasons and circumstances" for these revocations are not recorded in the nationality register.
They also added that decisions in citizenship matters are only recorded after they have become legally binding, so further entries may be added to previous years, for example, if legal action has been taken against a revocation order.
Why have revocations spiked?
Looking at the numbers above, it's apparent that the number of revocations of German citizenship has shot up significantly since 2024.
This is because in mid-2024 Germany reformed its Nationality Act to allow dual-citizenship for all nationalities. The reform also reduced the residency and language requirements for naturalisation.
Since then Germany has seen a dramatic increase in the number of foreign residents naturalising, and therefore also an increase in the number of citizenship revocations.
EXPLAINED: The different routes to obtaining a German passport
Before that, from 2021 to 2023, the number of revocations was relatively stable in the mid-100s range.
In 2020, the significantly smaller number of revocations may be at least partially explained by the Covid pandemic, and social-distancing measures which slowed down virtually all aspects of life.

“The Samota SEZ represents a strategic asset for Indonesia’s tourism, blending marine beauty, conservation wealth, and culture in one integrated area,” Deputy Tourism Minister Ni Luh Puspa said in a statement cited in Jakarta on Saturday.
During a meeting on plans for Samota in Sumbawa on Friday (July 24), she emphasized the ministry’s commitment to fostering an enabling environment for tourism investment in the SEZ through multiple measures.
Puspa highlighted efforts to streamline permit processes, build infrastructure to enhance attractions, strengthen the capacity of tourism professionals, and promote investment opportunities.
She explained that the government envisions the SEZ supporting the blue, green, circular, and creative economies, aiming to generate broader benefits beyond tourism growth.
The approach is designed to strengthen the fisheries sector; micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), livestock farms, and the agro-industry, paving the way for an interconnected economic landscape, she added.
Highlighting accessibility, Puspa noted that Samota is supported by Sultan Muhammad Kaharuddin Airport and Pototano Airport, which connect Sumbawa and Lombok and serve as gateways for domestic and international tourists.
The deputy minister argued that strong connectivity could help the SEZ attract both visitors and investment.
She further noted that the planned development comes amid a positive tourism trend in the region, with Sumbawa and Dompu Districts welcoming 514,419 and 497,048 visitors, respectively, during the January-October 2025 period.
On foreign tourist prospects, Puspa implied Samota’s potential to attract travelers arriving in Lombok through Zainuddin Abdul Madjid International Airport, mostly from Malaysia, Singapore, China, the United Kingdom, and France.
"The development of this zone is not narrowly oriented toward increasing tourist count; it is also directed to help create jobs, improve people's welfare, strengthen MSMEs, and attract long-term investment," she concluded.

items.title: Akuisisi Warner Bros Discovery Ditunda, Paramount Skydance Terancam Rugi 1,7 Miliar Dolar AS
items.summary: Akuisisi Warner Bros Discovery senilai 110 miliar dolar AS ditunda usai digugat 12 negara bagian AS karena diduga mengurangi persaingan.
items.body_text:
Akuisisi Warner Bros Discovery Ditunda, Paramount Skydance Terancam Rugi 1,7 Miliar Dolar AS
Akuisisi Warner Bros Discovery senilai 110 miliar dolar AS ditunda usai digugat 12 negara bagian AS karena diduga mengurangi persaingan.
Ringkasan Berita:
- Akuisisi Warner Bros Discovery oleh Paramount Skydance ditunda hingga pengadilan memutus gugatan antimonopoli dari 12 negara bagian AS.
- Penundaan ini berpotensi membuat Paramount menanggung biaya hingga 1,7 miliar dolar AS jika transaksi terus tertunda.
- Kasus tersebut menjadi ujian besar bagi pengawasan merger perusahaan media di Amerika Serikat.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM - Rencana akuisisi Warner Bros Discovery oleh Paramount Skydance senilai 110 miliar dolar AS resmi ditunda.
Kedua perusahaan sepakat menunggu putusan pengadilan atas gugatan antimonopoli yang diajukan 12 negara bagian di Amerika Serikat.
Penundaan itu disepakati setelah sejumlah negara bagian menggugat merger tersebut dengan alasan penggabungan dua raksasa media itu berpotensi mengurangi persaingan di industri hiburan dan membatasi pilihan konsumen.
Berdasarkan dokumen pengadilan, Paramount dan Warner Bros Discovery sepakat menunda penyelesaian transaksi hingga lima hari setelah hakim memutus perkara, atau paling lambat 1 Juni 2027, mana yang lebih dahulu tercapai.
Keputusan itu membuat Paramount menghadapi risiko finansial yang tidak kecil, Al Jazeera melaporkan.
Jika akuisisi belum rampung hingga batas waktu tersebut, perusahaan berpotensi membayar biaya yang telah disepakati kepada pemegang saham Warner Bros Discovery hingga 1,7 miliar dolar AS.
Selama proses penundaan berlangsung, Paramount juga diperkirakan harus menanggung biaya sekitar 7 juta dolar AS per hari.
Juru bicara Paramount menegaskan perusahaan tetap optimistis dapat memenangkan perkara tersebut.
"Kami berharap dapat membuktikan kasus kami di persidangan," kata juru bicara Paramount.
Reuters melaporkan, gugatan diajukan oleh 12 negara bagian AS yang dipimpin California pada 13 Juli 2026.
Mereka menilai merger tersebut berpotensi menghilangkan persaingan di Hollywood dan mengurangi pilihan masyarakat, terutama bagi penonton film maupun pelanggan televisi kabel.
Baca juga: Tok! Paramount Menangkan Persaingan Akuisisi Warner Bros, Netflix Makin Terdesak
Jaksa Agung New York Letitia James menyambut baik keputusan penundaan tersebut.
Menurutnya, penghentian sementara transaksi menjadi langkah penting untuk memastikan proses hukum berjalan sebelum merger bernilai raksasa itu disahkan.
Beberapa hari sebelumnya, Hakim Distrik Amerika Serikat Araceli Martinez-Olguin juga telah mengabulkan permintaan perintah penahanan sementara yang membekukan transaksi hingga persidangan berlangsung.

items.title: Komentar Owner Skincare soal Perseteruan Amanda Manopo dengan Eks Karyawan yang Diduga Lakukan Teror
items.summary: Tanggapan owner skincare soal perseteruan Amanda Manopo dengan eks karyawan yang diduga melakukan teror.
items.body_text:
Kabar Artis
Komentar Owner Skincare soal Perseteruan Amanda Manopo dengan Eks Karyawan yang Diduga Lakukan Teror
Tanggapan owner skincare soal perseteruan Amanda Manopo dengan eks karyawan yang diduga melakukan teror.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM - Aktris Amanda Manopo belum lama ini mendatangi Polda Metro Jaya, Jakarta guna berkonsultasi terkait permasalahannya dengan salah satu mantan karyawannya.
Hal itu terjadi setelah Amanda melakukan audit pada rekening perusahaan hingga mendapati aliran dana diduga kepada mantan karyawannya tersebut.
Tak tanggung-tanggung dalam hal ini, aktris pemilik nama lengkap Amanda Gabriella Manopo Lugue ini pun mengalami kerugian mencapai Rp3 miliar.
Tak hanya itu, Amanda kabarnya juga mengalami dugaan praktik dukun alias guna-guna, hingga ancaman pembunuhan dari mantan karyawannya.
Didampingi oleh kuasa hukumnya, Sandy Arifin, pihak Amanda Manopo pun akan melaporkan secara resmi mantan karyawannya itu pada pekan depan.
Permasalahan yang kini dialami bintang sinetron Ikatan Cinta ini pun mendapatkan tanggapan dari, pengusaha Rita Armila yang pernah bekerja sama dengan Amanda Manopo.
Lewat unggahan di Instagram pribadinya, Rita Armila mengungkap sisi lain dari Amanda Manopo yang tak banyak diketahui publik.
Di mana istri aktor Kenny Austin ini disebut memiliki hati yang baik dan kerap memberikan makanan kepada rekan kerjanya termasuk kru di lokasi syuting.
"Ingat banget pas dia (Amanda) spill total pesanan makanan online itu sampai berapa puluh juta gitu, katanya dia beli bukan untuk sendiri tapi untuk semua kru di lokasi syuting, dibeliin juga. Masya Allah nih anak beneran beb, ini kiriman dari salah satu kru aku yang kemarin juga ikut kita photoshoot bareng," kata Rita Armila dikutip Sabtu (25/7/2026).
Setelah mengungkap kebaikan hati dari aktris 26 tahun ini, Rita Armila pun memberikan sindiran untuk mantan karyawan yang kini berselisih dengan Amanda Manopo ini.
"Seharusnya bisa kerja sama seorang Amanda Manopo aja itu kayak udah poin gak sih? Seandainya itu posisi kalian, kalian nih bisa bekerja atau dipekerjakan sama seorang Amanda Manopo gitu kan. Harusnya udah bersyukur, tapi itulah kembali lagi ya, manusia tidak pernah cukup," tambahnya lagi.
Lewat kerangan dalam unggahan itu, pengusaha yang dijuluki sebagai Owner Ijo-ijo ini pun bersaksi soal kebaikan hati aktris kelahiran Jakarta, 6 Desember 1999 ini.
Baca juga: Amanda Manopo Bongkar Motif Eks Karyawan Lakukan Teror hingga Ancam Membunuh
"Aku dan team saksi sebaik apa Amanda Manopo, yang sudah pernah ketemu beliau pasti tau," tukasnya.
Rita Armila Ikut Terkena Imbas Konflik Amanda Manopo
Siapa sangka konflik antara Amanda Manopo dengan mantan karyawannya itu pun membuat Rita ikut terkena getahnya.
Di mana pengusaha skincare ini mendapatkan banyak hujatan setelah disangka sebagai mantan karyawan yang tengah berkonflik dengan Amanda.

Hari Mangrove Sedunia diperingati setiap tanggal 26 Juli yang tahun ini jatuh pada hari Minggu (26/7/2026).
Peringatan Hari Mangrove Sedunia 2026 adalah momen untuk meningkatkan partisipasi masyarakat dalam perlindungan dan pengelolaan mangrove berkelanjutan.
Dalam rangka peringatan Hari Mangrove Sedunia 2026, Kementerian Lingkungan Hidup/ Badan Pengendalian Lingkungan Hidup (Kemenlh/Bplh) membagikan Surat Edaran Menteri Lingkungan Hidup Nomor 10 Tahun 2026 tentang Peringatan Hari Mangrove Sedunia Tahun 2026.
SE Menteri Lingkungan Hidup berisi ajakan seluruh pemerintah daerah, dunia usaha, organisasi masyarakat sipil, komunitas, media massa, serta seluruh elemen masyarakat untuk berpartisipasi dalam aksi nyata pelestarian mangrove.
Pada peringatan Hari Mangrove Sedunia 2026, Kemenlh/Bplh mengangkat tema "Menjaga Mangrove, Mengamankan Generasi Mendatang."
Melalui tema itu Kemenlh mengajak semua pihak dalam momentum ini bersama untuk memperkuat kesadaran, kolaborasi, dan aksi nyata dalam perlindungan serta pengelolaan ekosistem mangrove yang berkelanjutan.
Selain tema, Kemenlh juga merilis Logo Hari Mangrove Sedunia 2026 yang menyimpan filosofi mendalam tentang perlindungan pesisir, mitigasi perubahan iklim, hingga kolaborasi lintas sektor.
Dari akar hingga burung yang terbang bebas, semua elemen mengajak kita untuk menyadari pentingnya sinergi antara alam dan manusia. 
Warna hijau melambangkan kehidupan, biru untuk keberlanjutan laut, cokelat untuk ketangguhan tanah, dan putih untuk keharmonisan masa depan. 
Partisipasi masyarakat dalam memperingati Hari Mangrove Sedunia 2026 terutama di era digital tidak cukup hanya dilakukan melalui kegiatan seremonial, tetapi juga dapat dilakukan melalui sosmed.

items.title: Still swinging: What’s next for Manny Pacquiao’s boxing career
items.summary: At 47, Manny Pacquiao does not plan to stop fighting anytime soon as the Filipino boxing icon eyes both professional and exhibition bouts, with the postponed rematch against Floyd Mayweather Jr. still in the cards
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
Father Time is undefeated, but Manny Pacquiao keeps resisting.
At 47, Pacquiao does not plan to stop fighting anytime soon — the Filipino boxing icon eyeing both professional and exhibition bouts through 2026 and 2027, with a long-awaited rematch against Floyd Mayweather Jr. still firmly on the agenda.
So what is next?
Top priority
According to Manny Pacquiao Promotions chief executive officer Jaspreet “Jas” Mathur, reviving the postponed Mayweather rematch is the priority.
Pacquiao and Mayweather, who first met in their blockbuster 2015 showdown, had agreed to face each other again in a professional fight scheduled for September to be streamed globally by entertainment giant Netflix.
A quick look at Netflix’s catalog shows the rematch remains on the platform’s schedule, but the fight has been postponed indefinitely due to legal and contractual disputes involving Mayweather’s camp.
“He has a long way to go. He’ll definitely be in a lot of exhibitions over the next few years but we ran into a little bit of a hiccup with the Mayweather fight that was initially planned for September of this year,” Mathur said of Pacquiao.
“Based of that, we didn’t entertain other exhibition offers that were there around. We’re also looking at the right partners to work for exhibitions, and then from there, also the right opponents for pro fight. There’ll be a lot of things coming up.”
“There’s a plan to have a fight for this year and then to roll into next year with the big fight.”
Mayweather has been embroiled in legal trouble after CSI Sports Events, which was contracted to produce the American’s exhibition against former world heavyweight champion Mike Tyson and rematch against Pacquiao this year, sued him for breach of contract.
CSI Sports Events claimed that Mayweather breached their agreement when he agreed to fight Greek kickboxer Mike Zambidis in an exhibition bout scheduled for June 27. The fight, however, never took place.
Mathur, though, said Mayweather was not to blame for the postponement of his rematch with Pacquiao.
“It’s just a very, very big mess and just a very complicated situation that was really caused by one person. For the record, this whole mess that happened is not really Floyd’s fault but we have to untangle it. There’s been a lot of work and his team is working, they’re doing what they need to do to untangle certain things,” said Mathur.
“Next year, 100 percent, it’s going to happen.”
By the time the rematch rolls around, however, Mayweather — who will turn 50 in February — and Pacquiao are far removed from the fighters who squared off in their 2015 clash famously dubbed the “Fight of the Century.”
The fight shattered revenue records by generating over $600 million, although the action in the ring proved underwhelming, with a defensive-minded Mayweather warding off Pacquiao to score a unanimous decision win and stay unbeaten.
Mayweather has fought professionally only twice since, beating Andre Berto in 2015 and Conor McGregor in 2017 to raise his record to 50-0 before retiring for the third time in his career.
For Mathur, having Pacquiao and Mayweather back in the ring together is still a sight to behold despite their age.
“Everybody wants to see Floyd and Manny one more time. That’s what’s going to break all records. That’s what’s going to be the most viewed event again in today’s era, in the streaming era,” he said.
“I think people are always going to be interested in watching that fight. These guys, they’re an anomaly, each one of them, whether Floyd or Manny. Age doesn’t really matter in that spectrum between these two. Everybody’s going to watch the fight. The people that say they’re not going to watch the fight are going to be the first ones to watch the fight.”
“Floyd’s not backing down from this, and neither is Manny.”

items.title: [OPINION] Para sa aking mga kapatid
items.summary: An INC member pens an open letter to his fellows: 'Ang hindi ko lang maunawaan, bakit ang imbestigasyon kay Pang. Ferdinand Marcos at kanyang mga kaalyado ay nararapat para sa hustisya at katotohanan, pero pagdating kay VP Sara Duterte at Sen. Rodante Marcoleta, ito ay panggigipit at pamumulitika lamang?'
items.body_text:
“Huwag kayong padaya kaninuman sa pamamagitan ng mga pangangatuwirang walang kabuluhan, sapagkat dahil nga sa mga ito, ang Diyos ay napopoot sa mga suwail. (…)
Sapagkat pawang mabuti, matuwid at totoo ang ginagawa ng namumuhay sa liwanag. Sikapin ninyong matutunan kung ano ang kalugud-lugod sa Panginoon.
Huwag kayong makibahagi sa mga gawain ng kadiliman na walang ibinubungang mabuti. Sa halip ay ibunyag ninyo ang mga iyon.”
Efeso 5:6, 9-11
– Excerpt from a weekend INC worship service, June 6, 2026
Bago ang lahat, nais kong humingi ng paumanhin.
Sa aking mga kaibigan, kakilala, at kapwa Pilipino na nalilito, naguguluhan, at nagagalit sa mga nagaganap.
Sa ating Panginoong Diyos, dahil sa lungkot, pangamba, at pagkadismaya na bumabalot sa atin.
At sa aking mga kapatid sa Iglesia Ni Cristo, mga taong lubos kong tinitingala ngunit kailangan kong tawagan ng pansin. Mahal ko kayong lahat, ngunit ito rin ang nagtulak sa akin para ihayag ang matagal ko nang napapansin.
Pinakinggan ko kayo noon. Sana’y mabigyan niyo rin ako ng pagkakataon ngayon.
Selective justice
“Dapat panagutin ang lahat ng mapatutunayang sangkot sa kurapsyon na yan, sinuman sila, anuman ang kanilang posisyon sa gobyerno, dapat silang panagutin.”
– Bro. Bienvenido Santiago Jr., INC General Evangelist at Rally for Transparency and a Better Democracy, November 16, 2025
Matapos malantad ang matinding katiwalian kaugnay ng flood control projects, sunod-sunod ang mga demonstrasyon na nananawagan sa imbestigasyon at pagpapanagot sa mga maysala. Isa ang INC sa mga nagsulong ng parehong layunin at nanawagan sa administrasyong Marcos na seryosohin ito.
Kaisang-diwa ako dito. Tama lang na ipaglaban ang katotohanan at katarungan.
Ang hindi ko lang maunawaan, bakit ang imbestigasyon kay Pang. Ferdinand Marcos at kanyang mga kaalyado ay nararapat para sa hustisya at katotohanan, pero pagdating kay VP Sara Duterte at Sen. Rodante Marcoleta, ito ay panggigipit at pamumulitika lamang?
Oo, mas malaki ang trilyones na nilimas sa flood control kumpara sa milyon-milyong hindi maipaliwanag na confidential funds o undeclared campaign donations, ngunit hindi ba’t dapat mabigyang-linaw ang parehong isyu? Bakit nagbabago ang pananaw natin, depende sa personalidad na nasasakdal?
Tayo na ang nagsabi: “Selective justice is INJUSTICE”
Muli, tama at makatarungan lang na kalampagin ang gobyerno na panagutin ang mga sangkot sa flood control corruption, ngunit ang panawagang ito ay mawawalan ng kredibilidad at magiging kaduda-duda kung isasantabi na lang ang iba pang isyu ng katiwalian.
Tayo ba ay para sa katotohanan at katarungan, o nais lamang ipagtanggol ang kaalyado at tuligsain ang kalaban?
Accountability
“Kaya natin sila pinili at ibinoto sa ating pag-aakala na sila po ay gagawa ng mabuti sa kapakanan po ng sambayanang Pilipino.
Pero sila po ang sumira sa pagtitiwala nating iyon.“
– Bro. Arnel Tumanan at EDSA Rally, July 1, 2026
Una, naniniwala ako na may mga kritisismo sa INC na paninira o pang-uusig lamang. Hindi ako sang-ayon sa mga gawa-gawang paratang, at umaasa ako na mabigyan rin sila ng pagkakataong maunawaan ang ating pananampalataya.
Ikalawa, hindi rin ako sang-ayon na wala tayong karapatang mag-rally gayong binoto natin sila. Constitutional right ng bawat mamamayang Pilipino na ihayag ang kanilang mga saloobin, at dapat lamang na singilin ang mga opisyal na pinagkatiwalaan natin.
Ngunit, naniniwala ako na maling ituring na pang-uusig kaagad ang lahat ng puna, lalo kung ito ay nakaaapekto na sa buong bansa.
Para ba talaga saan, o kanino, tayo tumitindig?
Mula Pagsamba ng Kabataan hanggang sa katandaan, laging pinapaalala ang kahalagahan ng katapatan at pananagutan. Hinahanap sa bawat kapatid ang mga katangiang nakasulat sa Bibliya, at handa tayong tawagan ng pansin ang mga pagkukulang sa layong maging sakdal at kalugod-lugod ang ating paglilingkod sa Panginoong Diyos.
Masigasig tayo sa loob ng Iglesia, pero ganito rin ba tayo para sa bayan?
Ang pandarambong ni Joseph Estrada, pandar

items.title: LTFRB studying expanded fuel discounts for PUVs amid Middle East tensions
items.summary: The LTFRB is considering expanding and increasing fuel discounts for public utility vehicles instead of approving a fare hike as oil prices continue to rise due to the unstable situation in the Middle East.
items.body_text:
LTFRB studying expanded fuel discounts for PUVs amid Middle East tensions
MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) said it is considering expanding and increasing fuel discounts for public utility vehicles (PUVs) as an alternative to a fare hike amid continued oil price increases driven by the unstable situation in the Middle East.
In a statement posted on its official Facebook page on Saturday, July 25, the LTFRB said discussions are ongoing with concerned government agencies and transport stakeholders to determine the best form of assistance for the public transport sector.
The agency said it is also reviewing and recomputing pending fare hike petitions as directed by Transportation Secretary Giovanni "Banoy" Lopez.
“We are factoring everything in the conduct of review and recomputation and this includes the fact that it is difficult to do so because the situation in the Middle East remains unpredictable and unstable,” LTFRB Chairman Vigor Mendoza II said.
Among the proposals being considered is expanding the existing P10-per-liter fuel discount to help offset the additional operating costs being raised by the PUV sector.
The LTFRB said the current fuel discount covers passenger jeepneys and UV Express units, which it described as among the country's most commonly used modes of public transportation.
More than 87,000 PUVs have already benefited from the fuel discount, while over 143,000 units have been listed in the program, according to the agency.
Mendoza said expanding and increasing the fuel discount is among the options under discussion, although it would require a larger government budget.
“We are looking into this proposal as the last option because the discussions on the matter are ongoing, and these discussions include public consultations with stakeholders nationwide,” he said.
Supporters of the proposal have argued that expanding the fuel discount would help transport operators cope with rising fuel prices without passing additional costs on to commuters through higher fares.
Mendoza said the proposal remains under consideration as the government weighs measures to cushion the impact of volatile global oil prices.
The LTFRB earlier committed to expedite discussions on pending fare hike petitions following Lopez's directive to review and recompute proposed fare adjustments.

items.title: Media, rights groups urge Congress to junk Marcos anti-disinfo bill
items.summary: Civil society groups and rights advocates are urging the Senate to defer pending anti-disinformation bills that they say borrow language from the Anti-Terrorism Act and hand the government powers that “may be weaponized by whoever holds office.”
items.body_text:
Media, rights groups urge Congress to junk Marcos anti-disinfo bill
MANILA, Philippines — Civil society groups and rights advocates are urging the Senate to defer pending anti-disinformation bills that they say borrow language from the Anti-Terrorism Act and hand the government powers that “may be weaponized by whoever holds office.”
The groups said they support action against disinformation — many of them having reported or been victimized by it — but argued the current bills only target small-time spreaders while going soft on social media companies.
"What the bill does is leave a sword of Damocles to frighten the free expression of the people," said Justin Daduya of Sigla Research Center during a public discussion of the bills with other civil society groups and media organizations.
“[While safeguard provisions] sound well on paper, as we’ve seen, for example, in the Anti-Terror Law, consistently these provisions don’t hold up when it comes to the implementation,” Daduya said.
The bill’s provisions, Daduya warned, are “easy to weaponize against normal activists or even news organizations that speak truth to power."
House Bill 9465, or the Digital Media Anti-False Information Act, hurdled third and final reading in June, some three months after being listed as a Marcos priority measure.
The bill lists as its author House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos, the president's eldest son. The measure passed 286-3 with seven abstentions.
Its Senate counterpart remains at the committee level under the Committee on Public Information and Mass Media, which has yet to have a new chair under Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. himself called on lawmakers in February to prioritize the anti-disinformation measure, saying it should be “balanced” and must not curtail freedom of expression.
Anticipating that Marcos could again push for the bill’s passage in Monday’s State of the Nation Address, at least a dozen civil society groups and media organizations released a joint statement on Saturday, July 25, opposing the measures.
Curtailing right to free speech
"These measures pose a far greater threat to the public's freedom of expression than to the disinformation economies they purport to dismantle," the coalition of advocates said in its joint statement.
Both bills extend criminal liability to those who "materially assist" disinformation — language the groups said parallels the terrorist financing provisions of the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020, which has "consistently been used for prosecution by association."
The Senate version criminalizes publishing content while merely "knowing or having a reasonable belief" of its falsity — "an incredibly low bar," according to the groups' joint statement.
The House version sets stricter standards, requiring actual knowledge of falsity and specific intent to cause verifiable public harm.
But the groups called these "empty words" that read well on paper while doing little to prevent legal harassment in practice.
Violators face six to 12 years in prison, with heavier penalties if the offender is a media personality — a provision Carlos Nazareno, director for rights at Democracy.net.ph, said could have a chilling effect on journalists.
"As shown in the dangerous cyber libel provisions in the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 and the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020, it is extremely difficult to repeal or amend bad laws in our country," Nazareno said. "Prevention is far easier than the cure."
Soft on platforms, hard on users
The coalition said neither bill has credible enforcement against the platforms that design and profit from disinformation.
Fines are “a drop in the bucket of big tech’s earnings,” and the House version includes a liability shield insulating companies unless they knowingly, actively, and materially participated in creating false content.
"Experience tells us that's an insurmountable bar,” Daduya said.

items.title: First tranche of P85 minimum wage hike begins in Metro Manila
items.summary: The first tranche of the approved P85 daily minimum wage increase in Metro Manila took effect on Saturday, granting a P60 pay hike to around 1.1 million minimum wage earners in the National Capital Region.
items.body_text:
First tranche of P85 minimum wage hike begins in Metro Manila
MANILA, Philippines — The first tranche of the approved P85 daily minimum wage increase in Metro Manila took effect on Saturday, granting a P60 pay hike to around 1.1 million minimum wage earners in the National Capital Region (NCR).
Under Wage Order No. NCR-27, the daily minimum wage for workers in the non-agricultural sector increased from P695 to P755.
Workers in the agriculture sector, service and retail establishments employing 15 workers or fewer, and manufacturing firms with fewer than 10 employees will now receive P718 a day, up from P658.
The remaining P25 increase will take effect on Jan. 20, 2027, raising the daily minimum wage to P780 for non-agricultural workers and P743 for workers in agriculture and covered small establishments.
The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) said the wage adjustment is the largest minimum wage increase granted in Metro Manila to date, with an estimated 1.1 million workers expected to benefit.
The labor department also reminded employers to comply with the wage order.
“In line with the implementation, the labor chief (Francis Tolentino) continues to remind employers to follow the wage adjustment, as non-compliance will result in penalties set by law," the DOLE said in a press release.
"He (labor chief Tolentino) also urged resolving wage distortion, or the adjustment of salaries above the minimum wage, through collective bargaining agreements between labor and management,” it added.
The increase took effect despite calls from the Foundation for Economic Freedom (FEF), a private-sector public advocacy group and think tank, to suspend the wage order, saying the increase could fuel inflation and eventually drive up the cost of goods and services.
Malacañang, however, rejected calls to defer the implementation. Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said the Palace had not received any formal request from the private sector to suspend or revoke the wage order.
The P85 wage increase will be implemented in two tranches, with the second and final P25 adjustment set to take effect on Jan. 20, 2027.

items.title: Province offers up to $40,000 for students winning international Olympiad gold medal, eight times Vietnam's GDP per capita
items.summary: Quang Ninh Province has set Vietnam's largest student prize at VND1.05 billion (US$39,900) for an international Olympiad gold medal, which is eight times Vietnam's 2025 GDP per capita of VND125.5 million.
items.body_text:
Quang Ninh's base award for an international gold is VND700 million ($26,600). It rises to VND1.05 billion for students who are from ethnic minorities or who live in designated ethnic minority, mountainous or island communes.
Silver pays VND500 million, bronze VND400 million and a certificate of merit VND200 million, under a resolution effective Aug. 1. Teachers who train a winner collect half the student's award.
The province also pays VND70 million for a national first prize, more than 17 times the state rate.
For scale, VND1.05 billion is more than a decade of earnings for the average Vietnamese worker, who made VND8.4 million a month last year, according to the national statistics office.
National rewards are far smaller, including VND55 million ($2,090) for an international gold, VND35 million for silver and VND25 million for bronze, with national-level prizes worth VND1 million to VND4 million.
Coming second among Vietnam's localities are Hai Phong, Ninh Binh and Bac Ninh which now pay VND500 million ($19,000) for an international first prize.
Da Nang is paying VND400 million, followed by Hanoi, Hue the Mekong Delta's Vinh Long with VND300 million, and Hung Yen and Tuyen Quang with VND250 million.
Ho Chi Minh City pays VND200 million for a top international prize.
The rewards were announced following Vietnam's strongest Olympiad season on record.
All six contestants medaled at the International Mathematical Olympiad in Shanghai from July 10 to 21, two of them with gold. Vietnam finished fifth among 119 countries and territories, up from ninth in 2025.
All four chemistry team members took gold in Tashkent, where 368 students from 93 countries and territories competed. Vietnam tied China and India for the most golds, and it was the fourth time since 1996 that every Vietnamese entrant won gold.
The physics team took four golds and a silver in Colombia, its best result, with two students scoring a perfect 30 out of 30 on the theory paper.
Vietnamese students earned 362 medals from regional and international Olympiads between 2016 and 2025, including 112 golds, according the Ministry of Education and Training. They were often among the competitions' top 10, with the chemistry team among the world's top 5 since 2020.

items.title: Hong Wang, third woman in 90 years to win math's highest honor, once left the field for architecture
items.summary: Hong Wang, who abandoned mathematics for a semester of architecture in Paris after deciding she was not good enough for research, has become the third woman to win the Fields Medal.
items.body_text:
Hiraku Nakajima, president of the International Mathematical Union and chair of the Fields Medal selection committee, presented the four medals at the Pennsylvania Convention Center in Philadelphia on July 23. The other recipients were Yu Deng of the University of Chicago, John Pardon of Stony Brook University and Jacob Tsimerman of the University of Toronto.
The union cited Wang's work in harmonic analysis and geometric measure theory, including the local smoothing conjecture for the planar wave equation, Fourier restriction, Falconer distance sets, Furstenberg sets in the plane and the Kakeya problem in three dimensions.
Wang is Silver Professor of Mathematics at New York University's Courant Institute and, since September 2025, a permanent professor at France's Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques. She is the first NYU faculty member to win the Fields Medal, the university said.
The medal has gone to a woman three times since it was first awarded in 1936. Maryam Mirzakhani, an Iranian mathematician at Stanford University, broke a run of 52 consecutive male recipients when she won in 2014 at 37, cited for her work on the dynamics and geometry of Riemann surfaces and their moduli spaces. She died of breast cancer in 2017, aged 40.
Maryna Viazovska, a Kyiv-born number theorist at the École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne, won in 2022, also at 37, for proving that the E8 lattice gives the densest possible packing of spheres in eight dimensions, a question open for more than 400 years.
Wang and Deng are the first Chinese nationals to take the award, the South China Morning Post reported. Shing-Tung Yau and Terence Tao, who won in 1982 and 2006, are ethnic Chinese but held other citizenships at the time.
Wang was born in 1991 in Pingle County, near Guilin in Guangxi, to parents who both taught at a local secondary school, and cruised through her early academic years with comfort.
She read Greek myths and Harry Potter, played table tennis and badminton, and worked through the exercises in each new textbook before term began because she wanted to, Quanta Magazine reported. She skipped two grades.
She entered the School of Earth and Space Sciences, at 16, on a college entrance exam score of 653. A geophysics professor pointed out how much mathematics underpins the science, including the seismic wave analysis used to map the Earth's interior, and she was eventually allowed to transfer to the School of Mathematical Sciences.
She graduated in 2011 and moved to France through a postbaccalaureate program at École Polytechnique. Her courses went well, but she did not believe she was capable of original research.
So she left, switched to architecture and took an internship at a Paris firm, where the pressure of mathematics lifted and her sense of purpose went with it. She returned within the semester, having decided to stop asking whether she would be good enough.
A research internship at MIT in 2013 put her in a seminar given by the analyst Larry Guth, whose explanation of his own recent proof she found clear enough to follow in part. She earned a master's degree at Université Paris-Sud in 2014, entered MIT's doctoral program the same year with Guth as her adviser and finished in 2019, then held a postdoctoral position at the Institute for Advanced Study, joined the UCLA faculty in 2021 and moved to NYU in 2023.
The problem she is best known for dates to 1917, when the Japanese mathematician Soichi Kakeya asked how little area a needle needs in order to turn and point in every direction. Abram Besicovitch showed by 1928 that the area can be made arbitrarily close to zero.
The modern conjecture concerns dimension rather than area, and Roy Davies proved the two-dimensional case in 1971. The three-dimensional version resisted every serious attempt for the next half century, defeating Jean Bourgain and Guth among others.
Wang and Joshua Zahl, then at the University of British Columbia, posted a 127-page proof of that case in February 2

items.title: Vietnamese Party and State leader honored with international peace prize
items.summary: General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV) Central Committee and State President To Lam has been named the laureate of the 2026 Lev N. Tolstoy International Peace Prize in recognition of his contributions to advancing peace and international cooperation.
items.body_text:
The jury unanimously voted on July 24 to confer the prestigious award on the Vietnamese leader, citing his role in "strengthening peace and cooperation among nations."
Participating in the jury meeting online from Saint Petersburg, jury chairman Valery Gergiev, General Director of the Bolshoi Theatre, Artistic Director and General Director of the Mariinsky Theatre, and a People's Artist of Russia, said Vietnam has emerged as one of the fastest-growing economies in the Asia-Pacific while preserving its distinctive cultural identity amid global integration.
The jury also recognized General Secretary and President Lam's contributions to Vietnam's development, his efforts to advance global justice and respect for international law, and his role in promoting the peace-loving, humane and dialogue-oriented traditions of the Party, government and people of Vietnam.
Other jury members, including Vladimir Tolstoy, Director General of the State Museum of L.N. Tolstoy and a descendant of the celebrated Russian author Lev Tolstoy, French public figure Pierre de Gaulle, and South African parliamentarian Lindiwe Sisulu, a member of the National Executive Committee of the African National Congress, highlighted the importance of safeguarding the universal humane values championed by Lev Tolstoy and other prominent historical figures.
They also commended Vietnam's development and international integration, saying the Southeast Asian nation, which was left largely devastated by war, has recovered and achieved remarkable economic growth, becoming an inspiration for many countries striving for peace.
The Lev N. Tolstoy International Peace Prize has now been awarded for the third time. The recipient is chosen by an international council of distinguished political, social and cultural figures from Argentina, Belarus, China, France, India, Japan, Russia and South Africa.

items.title: Italian embassy apologises for rowdy teens on BTS
items.summary: The Embassy of Italy on Saturday apologised to the Thai people over “the inappropriate behaviour of a group of Italian underage tourists” on a BTS Skytrain in Bangkok that generated heated conversations online, while strongly condemning their actions.
items.body_text:
The Embassy of Italy on Saturday apologised to the Thai people over “the inappropriate behaviour of a group of Italian underage tourists” on a BTS Skytrain in Bangkok that generated heated conversations online, while strongly condemning their actions.
The embassy’s Facebook page, which had been flooded with angry messages from Thai netizens, issued the apology in three languages — Italian, English and Thai.
It was responding to a viral video showing a Thai commuter confronting a group of young Italians for talking loudly and shouting inside a train carriage on Friday.
In the video, the Thai woman asked where they were from before telling them that shouting on the train was inappropriate, stressing that such behaviour was not common in Thailand.
The tourists appeared offended, and the situation escalated to rude gestures and profanity.
At one point, one member of the group said to the Thai woman, “Sorry for bringing money to your country.” Both parties exchanged profanities and insults throughout the video before the tourists disembarked.
In a statement on Saturday, the embassy expressed its deep regret over the incident, saying it “strongly condemns the inappropriate behaviour of the group”.
According to the embassy, the Italians seen in the video were underage tourists participating in a school educational trip.
“The Embassy extends its sincere apologies to the people of Thailand and to everyone affected by this incident,” it said. “Italians deeply understand and appreciate the values that Thai society places on respect for others, courtesy and harmonious coexistence — values that are equally cherished and upheld by the Italian Republic.”
The embassy said the group’s behaviour did not in any way represent the Italian people or reflect the values of mutual respect, friendship and courtesy that have long underpinned the enduring relationship between the Italian Republic and the Kingdom of Thailand.
It was later reported that messages from aggrieved Thais below an entirely unrelated Facebook post exceeded 10,000 before the embassy decided to disable comments.
Undeterred, some people decided to cast their outrage net abroad, targeting the social media accounts of Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.
In another post on the embassy’s Facebook page, a video showed four Italians, including one person seen in the original video, apologising to the Thai people and asking for forgiveness.
“We are very sorry to the people of Thailand because what we did on the BTS was wrong,” said one Italian teenager. “I’m very sorry for my behaviour.”
Earlier, the group’s Italian tour operator, TravellingFox, had also issued an apology. It said the group consisted of minors taking part in a study trip designed to discover a new culture, experience an international environment, and develop respect and openness towards the host country.

items.title: Criminal complaint filed in share-reporting case
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has filed a criminal complaint against a heretofore unknown investor for allegedly submitting false disclosure forms claiming ownership and trading of billions of baht worth of shares in six listed companies.
items.body_text:
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has filed a criminal complaint against a heretofore unknown investor for allegedly submitting false disclosure forms claiming ownership and trading of billions of baht worth of shares in six listed companies.
The affected companies were True Corporation, Kasikornbank, Bangkok Bank, Major Cineplex, Asia Aviation and GJ Steel.
The SEC said Supaporn Phimpong submitted four false director shareholding reports (Form 59) and seven substantial-shareholder reports (Form 246-2) between June 27 and July 2.
The filings claimed stakes worth more than 100 billion baht, including a reported 7% ]in True Corp, but the regulator found she had never owned or traded the shares.
The SEC flagged the filings after they appeared on its disclosure system, marked them as preliminary on July 3, changed their status to “under verification” on July 7 and removed them from public view on July 8 after confirming the information was false.
On July 10, the SEC and the police Economic Crime Suppression Division verified Ms Supaporn’s identity and took her statement. Further investigation led to the filing of the criminal complaint on Friday.
The case has attracted widespread attention from market observers who have raised concerns about the self-declaration disclosure system, which allows investors to report significant acquisitions before regulators verify the information.
The discrepancies also gave rise to speculation that the reporting system itself could have been compromised, hacked or somehow manipulated by parties linked to “grey money”.
The SEC said the alleged conduct violates Section 302/1 of the Securities and Exchange Act. The case will now proceed through a police investigation, prosecution and court proceedings, it said.
- EXPLAINER: Self-reporting scandal prompts reform calls
